Title: Sabah farmers urged to avoid open burning during Super El Nino
Article:
KOTA KINABALU: Farmers in Sabah have been advised against opening new agricultural areas during the expected 'Super' El Nino, said Sabah Agriculture, Fisheries and Food Industry Minister Datuk Jamawi Jaafar.
The phenomenon is expected to occur from September until January next year.
"For the next four to five months, we advise farmers not to open new agricultural areas.
"They are advised to focus on increasing water sources at their farms while avoiding open burning," Jamawi said after the recording of the Influencer@JAPEN Sabah programme here.
He also said 10,000ha of idle land for rice cultivation would be developed through a mini-estate approach involving private companies.
Jamawi said Sabah also aimed to increase padi yields to six to seven tonnes per hectare through mechanisation, suitable fertilisers and agricultural technology.
Currently, only 19 per cent of Sabah's rice requirements are met through local production, while the remainder is imported from Thailand, Vietnam and India.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: AHB Holdings sees substantial shareholder exit within two weeks
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: AHB Holdings Bhd saw City Popular Cash Sdn Bhd cease to be a substantial shareholder just two weeks after it emerged with a 10.87 per cent stake, held under a pledged securities account for Majestic Salute Sdn Bhd.
In a Bursa Malaysia filing today, AHB said City Popular disposed of 68 million shares through an off-market transaction on Aug 24, reducing its holding below the substantial shareholder threshold.
The filing did not disclose the identity of the buyer, the transaction price or the reason for the disposal.
Based on AHB's closing prices of four sen on Aug 21 and 4.5 sen on Aug 24, the 68 million-share block had a market value of between RM2.72 million and RM3.06 million
On Aug 18, AHB disclosed City Popular's emergence as a substantial shareholder after it acquired 99.78 million AHB shares in an off-market transaction on Aug 10.
The filings on both transactions did not identify the parties that sold or acquired the shares. It also remains unclear who is behind Majestic Salute.
Based solely on the two disclosed transactions, City Popular would have 31.78 million AHB shares remaining after the disposal.
At the time of writing, AHB shares were trading at four sen, down half a sen or 11.11 per cent, with 7.08 million shares changing hands.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Nepal flash flood kills eight; damages roads, power projects
Article:
KATHMANDU: Nepal sent helicopters to the rescue on Wednesday after a massive flash flood swept away villages in the Himalayan nation, killing eight and damaging roads, bridges and power projects in areas near Tibet, authorities said.
Across the border, Tibet reported "major casualties" with some missing in the neighbouring county of Gyirong after a mudslide hit a land crossing between China and Nepal, the Xinhua official news agency said.
The waters were too high for helicopters to land in Nepal's affected areas of Syapru Besi and Timure in the mountainous district of Rasuwa, with a population of about 50,000, officials said, while flagging the risk of casualties.
"There could be heavy casualties or loss of property," district administrator Narendra Pariyar told Reuters. "But I cannot say for sure now."
Pariyar urged those living on the banks of the Bhote Koshi river in the area to seek higher ground, pointing to reports that nearby villages and infrastructure project sites were washed away.
"It all came suddenly," the Onlinekhabar portal quoted a witness from the area as saying. "We heard a loud sound, like a volcano erupting. People started to scream and ran away."
Nepal's rescue helicopters would be unable to land in the affected areas until the waters recede, however, army spokesperson Raja Ram Basnet said.
[[nid:1519198]]
The cause of the inundation was not immediately clear, but a deadly flash flood on the same river last year was eventually traced to the draining of a glacier lake.
The mudslide on the Nepali side hit China's Gyirong port, Xinhua added, cutting off roads, communications and power in the Shigatse region near the border with Nepal, it added, without giving details.
President Xi Jinping urged "all-out" search efforts for the missing as well as stronger monitoring and early warning systems to prevent secondary disasters.
Nepal's energy ministry said 430 MW of electricity supplies were affected, mostly from hydroelectric projects, or more than 12 per cent of total national hydropower capacity of 3.2 GW, a Reuters calculation showed.
Prime Minister Balendra Shah said police and military were joining rescue and relief teams.
"Instructions have been given ... to move the people living in the lower areas to safer places," he said.
"People along the river are advised to exercise extra caution and remain alert."
From its origins in Tibet, the Bhote Koshi river empties into Nepal's Trishuli river that eventually flows into India as the Gandak river.
Last year's Bhote Koshi flood killed nine people, with 24 missing, as it washed away a 'Friendship Bridge' linking Nepal and China to disrupt trade and transport for months.
That flood was triggered by the draining of a supraglacial lake in Tibet, a regional climate monitor said.

Title: Pengerang peat blaze remains challenging despite water-bombing helicopter support
Article:
KOTA TINGGI: Firefighters had gained ground in tackling a peat fire along Jalan Bypass Punggai-Sebana Cove in Pengerang here by noon today, with a water-bombing helicopter deployed to support ground operations.
However, hot, dry and windy conditions continued to fuel the blaze and hamper efforts to contain it despite the aerial assistance.
Johor Fire and Rescue Department director Siti Rohani Nadir said the weather had caused the fire to spread rapidly, prompting firefighters to maintain round-the-clock operations to contain the flames and prevent further spread.
"Hot weather, dry conditions and strong winds have caused the fire to spread quickly," she said.
She said 27.8ha had been extinguished, leaving 23.6ha still affected.
Firefighters were conducting direct attacks in the two operational sectors, while excavators were being used to create firebreaks to cut off the fire's path.
A 15.8ha sector had been almost completely extinguished, with only inaccessible pockets of fire remaining.
These hotspots were being closely monitored to prevent them from flaring up again.
She said a helicopter had been deployed to the site to assist with water-bombing operations, providing aerial support over areas that were difficult for ground crews to reach.
Rohani also urged the public to be extra vigilant during the hot and dry spell, particularly by avoiding open burning and ensuring cigarette butts, matches and other flammable materials were properly extinguished and disposed of.
She said even a small ignition source could quickly trigger a fire under hot, dry and windy conditions.
"Avoid open burning and do not discard cigarette butts carelessly. Make sure any source of fire is completely extinguished before leaving the area," she said.
The fire along Jalan Bypass Punggai-Sebana Cove was first reported at 11.25am on Monday.
The affected area has since grown to 51.4ha, with the operation continuing non-stop to extinguish the remaining fire and prevent further spread.
No casualties have been reported.

Title: Farrah Naz conferred Datuk title
Article:
AYER KEROH: Media Prima Berhad News and Current Affairs Deputy Group Managing Editor Datuk Farrah Naz Abd Karim was among the recipients of the Melaka state awards, honours and medals presented in conjunction with the 77th birthday celebration of Yang Dipertua Negeri Melaka Tun Dr Mohd Ali Mohd Rustam today.
Farrah Naz, who is also New Straits Times Group Editor, was conferred the Darjah Pangkuan Seri Melaka (DPSM), which carries the title Datuk.
The award was presented by Mohd Ali at an investiture ceremony held at Balai Istiadat Seri Negeri here, witnessed by Chief Minister Datuk Seri Ab Rauf Yusoh.
Farrah Naz has more than two decades of experience in journalism and media management, having joined New Straits Times as a reporter in 2000 after completing her Bachelor's Degree in Mass Communications at Universiti Teknologi Mara.
She subsequently held several editorial positions at NST, including Putrajaya Bureau Chief, News Editor, Senior News Editor, Associate Editor (News and Current Affairs), NSTtv Editor and Executive Editor (Commercial).
She became New Straits Times Group Editor in September 2022 and was appointed Media Prima's Deputy Group Managing Editor (News and Current Affairs) in November 2024.
Farrah Naz currently also serves as deputy president of the Malaysian Press Institute (MPI), a member of the Bernama Supervisory Council and a board member of the Malaysian Media Council.
Her journalism career has been recognised with numerous awards, including the highest award in Malaysia, the Kajai Award in 2014 and 2015, MPI awards for investigative reporting and news reporting, and a 2017 World Association of Newspapers and News Publishers Silver Award for Best Newspaper Feature Article.
Among her other accolades are the Society of Publishers in Asia Award for Best Breaking News Reporting in 2016 for coverage of the assassination of Kim Jong Nam, as well as the 2024 NUJM Women Leadership Award.
In 2013, she received the Pingat Kedaulatan Negara for her coverage of the Lahad Datu incursion.
In 2025, Farrah Naz was conferred the Darjah Paduka Mahkota Perak.
In the final session of the investiture, Lembaga Tabung Angkatan Tentera chief executive officer Datuk Mohammad Ashraf Md Radzi was also conferred the DPSM.
Two other local media practitioners also received state honours. They are Melaka Hari Ini (MHI) Photo Unit head Iqmal Hakim Rosman and MHI journalist Liana Sahabudin.
They were each awarded the Pingat Jasa Kebaktian (PJK).
The awards presented today included one recipient of the Darjah Gemilang Seri Melaka (DGSM), 17 recipients of the Darjah Cemerlang Seri Melaka (DCSM), 62 recipients of the Darjah Pangkuan Seri Melaka (DPSM), 34 recipients of the Darjah Seri Melaka (DSM) and two recipients of the Jaksa Pendamai (JP).
The other recipients comprised 49 who received the Bintang Cemerlang Melaka (BCM), 90 the Bintang Khidmat Terpuji (BKT), 139 the Pingat Jasa Kebaktian (PJK), 58 the Bintang Bakti Masyarakat (PBM) and two the Pingat Khidmat Lama (PKL).

Title: Preacher, influencer claims trial to 51 charges involving RM15.4mil
Article:
SEREMBAN: A preacher and influencer today claimed trial at the Sessions Court here to 34 charges of criminal breach of trust (CBT) involving RM13.8 million belonging to a non-governmental organisation (NGO), and 17 money laundering charges involving RM1.56 million.
Abdullah Abdol Razak, 40, entered the plea after the charges were read before Sessions Court Judge Datin M Kunasundary.
On the 34 CBT charges, Abdullah, as an agent and chairman of Pertubuhan Rezeki Infaq Malaysia (Prim), was entrusted with RM13,847,535.89 in Prim funds.
He was accused of dishonestly disposing of the funds in breach of Clause 10 of Prim's constitution, which stipulates how the organisation's funds should be administered.
The alleged offences involved approving payments to several bank accounts, including his own, without authorisation from Prim's General Meeting.
The offences were allegedly committed between Feb 28, 2023 and March 31, 2026, at a bank in the district.
He was charged under Section 409 of the Penal Code, which carries a jail term of between two and 20 years, whipping and a fine upon conviction.
Abdullah also faces 17 money laundering charges involving RM1.56 million transferred from several bank accounts, including his own, to various accounts to purchase gold.
The offences were allegedly committed between May 18, 2024 and Feb 24, 2026, at the same location.
The charges were framed under Section 4(1)(b) of the Anti-Money Laundering, Anti-Terrorism Financing and Proceeds of Unlawful Activities Act 2001 (Act 613), punishable under Section 4(1) of the same Act.
Upon conviction, he faces up to 15 years in prison and a fine of not less than five times the amount or value of the proceeds of unlawful activity or RM5 million, whichever is higher.
Deputy public prosecutor Datuk Ahmad Akram Gharib said the offences were non-bailable but left it to the court's discretion to grant bail, proposing RM1 million.
He also proposed two Malaysian sureties, preferably non-family members, and additional conditions.
Defence lawyer Azrul Zulkifli Stork said his client was married and had 11 children aged between 4 and 15.
He said Abdullah also ran a restaurant and worked as an influencer, with an unstable income depending on his broadcasts.
Azrul said the proposed bail was excessive as all his client's bank accounts had been frozen.
He urged the court to set bail at RM700,000, comprising RM350,000 secured bail and the remainder unsecured.
The court granted bail of RM700,000 with two Malaysian sureties aged above 21, comprising RM400,000 secured bail and RM300,000 unsecured bail.
The court also ordered Abdullah to surrender his passport and barred him from interfering with prosecution witnesses, directly or through third parties.
Failure to comply with the conditions would result in the forfeiture of RM300,000 of the secured bail.
Meanwhile, Prim secretary Noor Sahira Abdullah, 30, was also charged with abetting Abdullah in committing CBT involving RM13,847,535.89 in Prim funds.
She was accused of intentionally assisting in transferring the funds through online banking to several bank accounts without authorisation from Prim's General Meeting.
The offence was allegedly committed between April 24, 2023 and March 28, 2026.
She was charged under Section 109 of the Penal Code, read together with Section 409, which carries a jail term of between two and 20 years, whipping and a fine upon conviction.
Deputy public prosecutor Syairah Aqilah Khalil offered bail of RM250,000 with two Malaysian sureties, subject to additional conditions.
Azrul, who also represented Noor Sahira, said she was married and had a five-month-old child and was supporting her ailing parents.
He urged the court to reduce the bail to RM150,000 with two sureties.
The court set bail at RM200,000 with two local sureties aged above 21, subject to the same additional conditions.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Industry body hails Anwar's call for greater creative freedom in films
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The Communications and Multimedia Content Forum of Malaysia (CMCF) has welcomed Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim's call for Malaysian filmmakers to be given greater creative freedom.
It said this should come with stronger self-regulation, clearer content classification and better parental controls.
Anwar had called for a freer, more open space for
local filmmakers
at the opening on Aug 24, while stressing that creative expression must remain grounded in Malaysia's values, culture and morality.
Its chairman and Media Prima group managing director Datuk Rafiq Razali said clear standards would give creators and investors more confidence to experiment and invest.
"Clear standards are important because when the expectations and boundaries are understood, creators are more confident about exploring bolder ideas.
"At the same time, the industry must show that greater freedom comes with responsibility," he said in a statement.
CMCF also welcomed the more progressive direction taken by the National Film Development Corporation Malaysia (Finas) and the Film Censorship Board (LPF), including greater reliance on age classification, which it said gives filmmakers more room while keeping audiences informed.
CMCF vice-chairman and Film Directors' Association of Malaysia chairman Datuk Afdlin Shauki said filmmakers needed room to tell difficult or sensitive stories that reflect real life.
"The key is to give audiences clear information about what they are watching and who it is suitable for, while giving filmmakers enough space to tell their stories honestly and responsibly," he said.
CMCF said safeguards for children should not depend on parents alone and called for platforms to offer easy-to-use features such as child profiles, PIN controls and content filters.
CMCF chief executive officer Mediha Mahmood said parents also needed to take age ratings more seriously.
"We still see children being taken to watch films that are not suitable for their age, even though exposure to certain material can have a harmful impact," she said, adding that ratings and parental controls should be made clearer and easier to use.
CMCF said it was prepared to convene filmmakers, broadcasters, streaming platforms, regulators and child-safety experts to explore an approach that gives creators more room while keeping audiences protected.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Govt focused on TH RCI follow-up, not new probes, says Zulkifli
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The government's priority following the declassification of the Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI) report on Tabung Haji (TH) is to ensure its findings are acted upon firmly and comprehensively.
Minister in the Prime Minister's Department (Religious Affairs) Dr Zulkifli Hasan said the government respected the Public Accounts Committee (PAC) as a credible parliamentary institution and was prepared to provide full cooperation if required.
However, he said the immediate focus should be on following up on the RCI's findings, in line with His Majesty Sultan Ibrahim, King of Malaysia's
decree
that all wrongdoing be thoroughly investigated.
"The Madani government pledges to carry out this trust with full responsibility and a sense of accountability before Allah, ensuring that every wrongdoing is addressed in accordance with the law," he said in a statement today.
Zulkifli said the RCI had strong institutional foundations, with its six members comprising experts in the judiciary, public administration, banking, Shariah and auditing.
He said the members were appointed with the consent of Al-Sultan Abdullah Ri'ayatuddin Al-Mustafa Billah Shah, the 16th King of Malaysia, in July 2021.
The composition, he said, ensured that the commission's investigations and recommendations were conducted independently, professionally and with full integrity.
He also said sustained public pressure for transparency over TH's management of Muslim savings since 2019 underscored the need for absolute accountability, with no room for compromise.
Yesterday, Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi said the PAC should
establish a special body
to investigate TH's management from 2017 to the present.
Zahid, who is also Umno president, said the move was necessary to establish the facts surrounding TH's management after 2017 and help correct public perceptions about the fund's issues.
Meanwhile, Perikatan Nasional secretary-general Datuk Seri Takiyuddin Hassan called for a new RCI into TH, alleging that the previous report's findings had been used to portray the agency as having been embroiled in a major financial scandal.
Umno Supreme Council member Datuk Mohd Razlan Rafii also supported establishing a new RCI to investigate TH's financial affairs after the previous inquiry.
The RCI into TH, established in January 2022 to investigate the management and operations of the pilgrims' fund between 2014 and 2020, was completed in July 2022.
The report revealed political interference, creative accounting practices, hibah payouts beyond the fund's means and poor investment decisions between 2014 and 2020.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Aroundtown's half-year profit more than halves on falling property prices
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Aroundtown, one of Germany's largest listed landlords, said on Wednesday its profit in the first six months of the year dropped by more than a half, as German commercial property prices fell in the second quarter.
It reported a net profit of €218 million (US$254 million) for the first half of 2026, down 62 per cent from a year ago, due to a lower valuation result and higher financing costs.
The property group also posted funds from operations, or FFO I, of €144 million, down from last year's €150 million.
Aroundtown had in April guided for its annual FFO I, a key metric measuring real estate firms' operating performance, to come between €275 million and €305 million.
It confirmed that guidance on Wednesday.

Title: Tan: Investors turn to collectable art as property market cools
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Investors are increasingly turning to collectable art as an alternative to property while waiting for the real estate market to recover or reach its bottom, according to Henry Butcher Real Estate Sdn Bhd chief operating officer Tang Chee Meng.
"Rather than moving away from property entirely, today's investors simply have a broader selection of asset classes to choose from, including stocks, art, fine wine, cryptocurrency, and even collectibles like premium Chinese tea," Tang said.
"Many of these alternative options carry price tags in the thousands of ringgit, yet artwork at recent auctions has drawn noticeably stronger interest," he told NST Property.
Tang said rising attendance at art auctions, where collectable pieces can range from about RM10,000 to RM600,000, points to growing interest in alternative assets, particularly when high-quality works by established artists come to market.
He said Malaysia's property market was entering a more cautious phase as developers faced mounting construction costs and greater uncertainty over project viability.
He said the combination of higher crude oil prices, elevated material costs and ongoing conflicts overseas was putting pressure on developers' margins and making new project launches a more carefully considered decision.
"Developers, particularly those without strong balance sheets, risk being caught between weaker-than-expected sales and rising construction costs once a project is launched.
"Unless developers are very confident of the sales prospects of a project, they will be very careful about launching," he said.
He said the concern is that developers may commit to construction contracts at current prices, only to face higher building material and other input costs later.
"If sales are slow while construction costs continue to rise, developers can get caught in between. In some cases, projects may even be delayed or abandoned halfway," he said.
As a result, developers are increasingly adopting a wait-and-see approach rather than rushing new projects to market.
The market, however, is not in a downturn, with demand still evident for well-located properties that are priced appropriately.
"People are cautious. They are waiting to see what happens before making a commitment. If a project comes into the market with a good location and the pricing is right, buyers will still buy," Tang said.
He said this selective buying behaviour is particularly evident in the higher-priced segment, where buyers have greater flexibility to defer purchases.
Political uncertainty could further reinforce that caution, with the 16th General Election (GE16) expected to be another factor that some buyers may want to assess before committing to major property purchases, he said.
At the same time, the current environment is creating opportunities for cash-rich developers.
Tang said with the broader market less aggressive, financially stronger developers can take advantage of opportunities to acquire strategically located land that may have been difficult or prohibitively expensive to secure during a property boom.
"Cash-rich developers are taking the opportunity to acquire well-located land, which they may not have been able to do when the market was very hot," he said.
He said that landed properties in established and sought-after locations remain among the more resilient segments, although buyers are becoming more deliberate in their decision-making.
He said the result is a market that is neither in outright decline nor displaying the exuberance of previous cycles.
"Instead, developers and buyers are watching each other closely, with developers reluctant to launch without sufficient sales visibility and buyers prepared to wait until location, pricing and broader economic conditions provide enough confidence to act," Tang said.
For now, caution rather than contraction is defining Malaysia's property market, he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Meta faces possible US$200b penalty as settlement talks emerge
Article:
SAN FRANCISCO: Social media giant Meta has been in discussions with multiple US states to settle a major child privacy and consumer protection case out of court, Bloomberg News reported on Tuesday.
With more than three billion users around the world, Meta is fending off accusations by a coalition of 29 states that it deliberately designed its products to hook children and gather their data while misleading the public.
The states are claiming that Meta violated both state-level and federal laws, though the exact allegations vary by state.
If Meta loses the case, the states could ask for around US$200 billion in penalties, in addition to forcing the tech company to make changes to its products.
"Meta Platforms Inc. and state attorneys general have discussed a possible mid-trial settlement," Bloomberg reported, citing anonymous sources familiar with the matter.
California, Colorado, New Jersey and Kentucky are leading the prosecution of Meta from a courtroom in Oakland, just a short drive from San Francisco.
Multiple state attorneys general sent out media advisories late Tuesday that they would hold press conferences on Wednesday regarding consumer protections and tech-related announcements.
Colorado said it would announce "a major update in a Big Tech case."
Nevada, which is not involved with the trial in California, said it would make an announcement Wednesday regarding a "settlement" with "a leading technology company."
Representatives for Meta and California Attorney General Rob Bonta did not immediately respond to a request for comment.
Instagram boss Adam Mosseri took the stand on Tuesday as the trial entered its second week.
Mosseri admitted he touted newly launched safety tools for teens without disclosing low adoption rates from early testing several years ago.
Other witnesses have testified over the past week that Meta knew these tools were not effective and even that they were "designed to fail."
Meta founder and chief executive Mark Zuckerberg was expected to testify at some point, as well.--AFP
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Maternity ward inferno kills 14 infants in Pakistan
Article:
ISLAMABAD: A fire erupted in a hospital maternity ward in Islamabad on Wednesday killing 14 infants, Pakistan authorities said, blaming a faulty air conditioner for the blaze.
The dawn fire broke out on the third floor of the Mother and Child Health Ward at the capital's premier public hospital Pakistan Institute of Medical Sciences (PIMS), the Islamabad district office said in a statement.
The statement gave a death toll of 14, who according to Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif were all infants.
Witnesses described chaotic and harrowing scenes, including intense smoke and broken glass, a slow response from emergency services and guards reportedly preventing them from leaving the ward.
Khurram Mehmood, 40, told AFP he lost his three-day-old daughter in the blaze and that rescuers took hours to arrive.
"My wife was in the ward. They took everyone out. We were sitting on the road waiting for help," he said.
The door to the neonatal intensive care unit was locked, according to Jaweria, a woman who said she lost her infant in the blaze.
"I do not believe this. Give me my child back... Why did the doctors leave the children there?"
"The fire spread very quickly. There were babies as young as one-day old," witness Abdul Ghafoor told AFP, adding that he went into the hospital to save patients but could not reach the maternity ward.
"There was thick black smoke inside and patients were trapped... Rescue teams arrived after almost two hours (since the fire started)."
Sohail Ashraf, the Islamabad chief commissioner, said the emergency call was made just before 7am (0200 GMT), with rescue and police teams reaching the scene "immediately" and bringing the fire under control.
Another witness, who did not gave her name, said hospital security "were not letting them out and the guards were stopping them."
"People had to break the door down and rescue teams had to break the windows to control the fire," she added.
- 'RAN FOR OUR LIVES' -
AFP reporters saw a nurse call out the names of babies who had perished in the fire as families gathered outside.
Other patients streamed outside, their faces covered in soot, with one man holding a newborn in his arms.
A mother with black residue from the smoke on her hands stood crying outside the hospital as she held her 10-day-old baby in her arms.
"People were screaming. There was black smoke. We ran for our lives. Thank god my baby is safe," Shagufta Parveen, the mother, told AFP.
An AFP reporter saw other families in tears and a man clear glass from two broken windows, as security guards stood at the entrance to the leading medical facility.
Prime Minister Sharif and Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi expressed "deep grief and sorrow over the deaths of 14 infants" in separate statements.
"The circumstances that led to the incident should be thoroughly reviewed, those responsible should be identified and the strictest possible action should be taken," the prime minister said.
PIMS spokeswoman Aneeza Jalil told AFP the fire was caused by an electrical fault, and "fire sparked from the AC."
Fires in large buildings are frequent in Pakistan, often due to poor safety laws and building codes as well as lax enforcement.
In January more than 65 people were killed in a shopping centre fire in the port city of Karachi.
At least 11 people were killed in another shopping mall fire in Karachi in 2023.
In 2021 at least 16 workers died after a factory fire in the same city.
In 2012 at least 250 labourers died at a garment factory in Karachi.--AFP
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Army strengthens capabilities against cross-border threats
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The army is strengthening its capabilities to counter non-conventional threats, including smuggling, intrusion, human trafficking, illegal logging and poaching.
Army Headquarters Strategic Transformation director Colonel Ahmad Nirman Fariz Zakaria said such threats included the movement of illicit goods such as drugs and firearms, which could contribute to rising crime rates.
"The smuggling of subsidised and controlled goods, whether into or out of the country, causes leakages that result in losses to national revenue," he said on Bernama TV's Apa Khabar Malaysia programme today.
He said human trafficking along Malaysia's borders also posed social and demographic security risks, while Sabah's east coast faced maritime threats including piracy and kidnapping for ransom.
Malaysia also faced natural resource theft along the peninsula's northern borders and areas bordering Kalimantan, including encroachment into forest reserves, illegal logging and poaching that threatened the country's flora and fauna.
"During the insurgency era, the army focused on hunting communist terrorists who used dense forests and border areas to organise their movements and evade security forces.
"Threats are constantly evolving, and the army will continue adapting its capabilities to address them," he said.
Ahmad Nirman said the army conducted operations independently and jointly with the Royal Malaysian Navy, Royal Malaysian Air Force and other security agencies, as well as Indonesian and Thai security forces, to safeguard the country's borders.
Technology such as drones, sensors, tactical communications equipment and digital intelligence analysis had also enhanced surveillance and monitoring capabilities along border areas, he said.
However, he said that personnel remained central to effective security operations, particularly given the challenging terrain and environment along Malaysia's borders.
In conjunction with National Day, Ahmad Nirman urged Malaysians to be the government's "eyes and ears" by supporting efforts to combat cross-border crime and working with the Malaysian Armed Forces to safeguard the country's sovereignty for future generations.
"Soldiers deployed along the borders face difficult terrain, extreme weather, remote locations, limited basic amenities and communications, while spending months away from their families.
"The public should therefore continue to support and appreciate their sacrifices in defending the country's sovereignty," he added.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Taxi driver jailed six years for ramming, killing Rohingya passenger
Article:
MUAR: A taxi driver who rammed and killed a Rohingya passenger during a dispute over an unpaid fare was jailed six years and fined RM20,000 by the High Court here today.
The court also ordered R. Dhana Balan, 31, to serve an additional year in prison if he failed to pay the fine.
Judge Kalyana Kumar Sockalingam imposed the sentence after accepting Dhana's guilty plea to an alternative charge under Section 41(1) of the Road Transport Act 1987.
The provision carries a maximum 10-year jail term and a fine of up to RM50,000.
Dhana was initially charged under Section 302 of the Penal Code with causing the death of the Rohingya passenger by driving dangerously.
The incident occurred between 6.50am and 7am on Oct 20, 2022, at Kilometre 16 of Jalan Kluang-Ayer Hitam near Sri Gading, Batu Pahat.
The victim had travelled from Johor Baru to Batu Pahat with his nephew in Dhana's taxi on Oct 19, 2022.
After reaching Batu Pahat, Dhana asked for the fare, but the victim said he did not have enough money.
The victim then offered four mobile phones from his bag to make up the shortfall, prompting Dhana to question whether the phones belonged to him or had been stolen.
An argument followed, with Dhana stopping the taxi by the roadside and ordering the victim and his nephew to get out.
The dispute then escalated into a fight, with the victim wielding a metal rod while Dhana armed himself with a piece of wood.
Dhana subsequently returned to his taxi and reversed at speed, hitting the victim as he tried to protect his nephew.
The victim fell unconscious and was later pronounced dead.
Deputy Public Prosecutor Siti Asmah Zainal Ariffin prosecuted, while Dhana was represented by lawyer Chelva R. Suppiah.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Alliance Bank Q1 earnings up 25pct as credit loss allowances fall
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Alliance Bank Malaysia Bhd's net profit rose 25 per cent in the first quarter ended June 30, 2026, driven by lower allowances for expected credit losses and higher revenue, partly offset by increased operating expenses.
Net profit increased to RM248.32 million from RM198.69 million a year earlier, while revenue grew 2.5 per cent to RM630.93 million from RM615.32 million, according to its Bursa Malaysia filing.
The higher revenue was supported by growth in both net interest income (NII) and non-interest income (NOII).
NII rose 2.5 per cent year-on-year to RM511.7 million, mainly on higher loan volumes, while net interest margin stood at 2.26 per cent. NOII also increased 2.5 per cent to RM119.2 million.
Operating expenses rose 7.8 per cent, reflecting continued strategic investments in technology and talent under its Acceler8 strategy.
Gross loans expanded 8.1 per cent year-on-year to RM67.81 billion, while total gross loans and unrated bonds grew 9.5 per cent to RM69.33 billion, outpacing industry loan growth.
Alliance Bank group chief executive officer Kellee Kam said the quarter's performance reflected the momentum of its Acceler8 strategy and the bank's ability to capture quality growth across its core segments.
He said the bank remained cautious in navigating the operating environment while continuing to gain market share in the small and medium enterprise and consumer banking segments, alongside sustained momentum across its regional franchises.
"As we enter the final stretch of Acceler8, we remain focused on investing prudently in our people, technology and capabilities, deepening customer relationships and delivering responsible, long-term value to all our stakeholders," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Prisons Dept to cooperate in probe into death in Marang prison
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The Prisons Department will give full cooperation to police investigating the death of an inmate who was allegedly assaulted by several fellow prisoners at Marang Prison.
In a statement today, the department said it had taken note of the incident, in which the inmate lost consciousness after being assaulted by several other inmates.
The incident occurred on Aug 24, with prison authorities receiving information before immediately sending the 38-year-old victim to Merchang Health Clinic for medical examination and further treatment.
However, a medical officer later confirmed that the inmate had died.
The department said the victim's body was subsequently sent to the Forensic Department of Hospital Sultanah Nur Zahirah (HSNZ), Kuala Terengganu, for a post-mortem examination.
"The Prisons Department confirms that the authorities are conducting an investigation into the incident.
"The investigation also covers the cause of the incident and the identification of those involved," it said.
Police had earlier said the victim was believed to have been assaulted by three fellow inmates, aged between 21 and 35, in a room at the prison.
Initial investigations indicated that the incident was believed to have stemmed from an old debt and dissatisfaction with the victim.
The three suspects, who are also from Terengganu, have been detained and are being investigated under Section 302 of the Penal Code.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: 3 more men remanded over illegal motorcycle race on Johor Second Link
Article:
KULAI: Three men have been remanded over an illegal motorcycle race on the Second Link highway in Johor, bringing the total number of arrests to 11.
One of the three men was remanded for four days, while the other two were ordered to be held for a day to assist investigations.
A 33-second video showing two motorcyclists
racing went viral
after several people blocked part of the highway in Johor last Saturday to allow the riders to race.
The men, aged between 24 and 41, were arrested at a condominium in Sentul, Kuala Lumpur, early today and are being investigated under Section 42(1) of the Road Transport Act 1987.
Bukit Aman Traffic Enforcement and Investigation Department director Datuk Seri Mohammed Hasbullah Ali said police believed a
RM15,000 bet
was placed on the illegal motorcycle race.
The footage also showed firecrackers being set off to celebrate the end of the race, while spectators gathered along the road shoulder to watch.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Umno denies 'charade' to shield those behind TH scandal
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Umno secretary-general Datuk Dr Asyraf Wajdi Dusuki has rejected allegations that the party staged a "charade" to shield those responsible for financial misconduct at Lembaga Tabung Haji (TH).
The response follows criticism from Jelutong Member of Parliament RSN Rayer, who accused Umno of organising a political spectacle to protect individuals involved in the alleged mismanagement of the pilgrims' fund.
"Umno has been consistent in our position: we will never condone, defend, or protect anyone found to have committed wrongdoing, whether in the TH issue or any other matter involving public institutions and funds," Asyraf said in a statement.
He stressed the importance of distinguishing between demanding accountability and creating a public perception of guilt before facts are established.
"The court of public opinion cannot be allowed to replace the court of law.
"Allegations, political narratives, and selective interpretations should not be treated as proof of criminal wrongdoing," he said.
Asyraf defended a recent forum on the matter, denying it was a "charade."
He said the inclusion of former Auditor-General Tan Sri Dr Madinah Mohamad and former Treasury secretary-general Tan Sri Dr Mohd Irwan Serigar Abdullah as panellists allowed different perspectives and facts to be presented openly.
"If there is credible evidence of wrongdoing, let it be investigated thoroughly and independently, and let those responsible face the full force of the law.
"But equally, we should not prejudge individuals or manufacture a perception of guilt merely for political mileage," he said.
He maintained that Umno's position remains straightforward.
"No cover-up, no protection for wrongdoers, but also no trial by political rhetoric or public perception," he said.
Earlier, Rayer had described the forum as an
"Umno sandiwara (charade)"
intended to shield those responsible for the alleged financial misconduct.
Rayer warned that politicising the RCI findings could erode public trust in the country's institutional integrity.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: [UPDATED] PAC to begin probe into TH governance, financial and investment weaknesses
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The Parliament's Public Accounts Committee (PAC) today unanimously agreed to begin proceedings into governance, financial and investment weaknesses at Lembaga Tabung Haji (TH).
PAC chairman Datuk Wira Mas Ermieyati Samsudin said the decision followed findings in the Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI) report into TH's management and operations from 2014 to 2020, which was made public on July 29.
She said the proceedings were not intended to duplicate the RCI's comprehensive investigation, but would focus on the actual status and progress of implementing its recommendations, in line with PAC's core function.
"PAC considers the disclosure of the RCI to be very serious and capable of eroding the confidence of Muslims in the country if it is not properly addressed.
"Several questions remain after the RCI report was made public and subsequently debated in the Dewan Rakyat during the special sitting on Aug 11," she said in a statement today.
Mas Ermieyati said as a bipartisan Parliamentary Select Committee, PAC had a clear mandate under the Standing Orders of the Dewan Rakyat, Treasury Instructions and General Circular No. 1 on the organisation of ministries and departments under the Prime Minister's Department to initiate proceedings on the matter.
"However, the title, terms of reference and list of witnesses for the LTH proceedings have yet to be determined.
"PAC will hold a special meeting to discuss these matters," she said.
Mas Ermieyati said PAC had experience investigating major and sensitive issues, including the 1Malaysia Development Bhd (1MDB) proceedings in 2016, the RM19.4 billion Goods and Services Tax (GST) refund arrears in 2019 and the procurement of the Royal Malaysian Navy's second-generation Littoral Combat Ships (LCS) in 2022.
She said the LCS proceedings were initiated after PAC received a report from the Government Governance, Procurement and Finance Investigation Committee in 2019.
To ensure a comprehensive, transparent and accountable investigation, she said, PAC would also refer to the RCI report, Auditor-General's reports and PwC audit reports during its proceedings.
"PAC is committed to conducting the investigation transparently and fairly to ensure continued accountability in the management of public funds and restore depositors' full confidence in TH," she said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Mi Technovation unit gets nod for Singapore listing
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Mi Technovation Bhd's unit, Mi Material Holding Ltd, has received approval to list on the Singapore Exchange.
In a filing with Bursa Malaysia, the company said Mi Material's eligibility-to-list approval is valid for three months from Aug 25, subject to conditions imposed by the Singapore Exchange.
Mi Technovation will retain an equity interest of about 72.6 per cent in Mi Material following the listing.
In a separate filing, Mi Technovation said the listing would enhance Mi Material's recognition and corporate stature.
It added that the separation of Mi Material from Mi Technovation would also allow for a "clearer segregation" of business responsibilities and operations among the group's business units.
Mi Technovation's shares rose 19 sen, or 3.13 per cent, to RM6.26 at 3.30pm, valuing the company at RM5.63 billion.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Critical illness can cost Malaysians up to RM1.2mil, says Allianz Life
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Treatment for critical illnesses and related expenses can cost between RM800,000 and RM1.2 million in complex cases, according to Allianz Life Insurance Malaysia Bhd.
Chief executive officer Giulio Slavich said the financial burden extended beyond medical bills, with patients potentially facing caregiver costs, loss of income and prolonged treatment.
"Critical illness cases are ranging around RM1 million. A little bit less, a little bit more, you see the range between RM800,000 and RM1.2 million," he said.
Data from Allianz Life showed that benefit payouts for cancer-related critical illness claims have increased 29 per cent since 2022, while payouts for stroke and heart disease have risen 95 per cent and 22 per cent, respectively.
Cancer is currently the leading diagnosis for critical illness claims at Allianz, with breast and colon cancers among those showing steady increases.
Slavich said the data pointed to a false sense of security among some Malaysians and an underestimation of the overall financial burden of dealing with critical illness.
"You have there the different type of diseases they went through and a little bit the cost amounts that have affected these people.
"So overall, let me say, putting these elements together, I would say there is a false sense of security out there.
"There is an underestimate of what this whole journey can overall cost and this is unluckily combined with the fact that there is actually this very, let me say, big increase in critical diseases in even younger ages," he said.
He said one in five Malaysians could face financial hardship due to medical expenses, while six in 10 could have difficulty raising RM1,000 in an emergency.
Slavich said the figures highlighted the country's protection gap, particularly as the financial burden could continue well beyond hospitalisation.
"We obviously have to take into consideration also that there can be some ongoing treatment well beyond what is happening during the moment in which actually the person is going through hospitalisation.
"So if you sum up all these elements, there can be high expenses, there can be income loss, and this is very scary.
"One in five actually as I was suggesting, can go broke because of this kind of deals, and actually we have put here a few numbers 2.1 billion people on the planet are actually lacking in adequate health coverage," he said.
Slavich said the situation was becoming more concerning amid rising medical inflation, which could further increase the cost of treatment and recovery.
He was speaking at Allianz Life's "Beyond Survival: The Journey from Setback to Comeback" forum, which also featured chief claims and health solutions officer Tammy Lee and National Cancer Society Malaysia (NCSM) managing director Prof Dr Muralitharan Munisamy.
Lee said cancer was the most common critical illness claim received by Allianz, with at least 30 per cent of its cancer cases involving cancers affecting women.
She said cancer was also increasingly affecting younger people, while many patients continued to be diagnosed at later stages of the disease.
Muralitharan said almost two-thirds of cancers in Malaysia were detected at late stages, with about 95 per cent of lung cancer cases diagnosed at Stage 3 or 4.
He said late detection not only reduced survival prospects but also significantly increased treatment costs.
Meanwhile, Allianz Life has launched HealthCover Prime, a health protection solution designed to provide broader financial protection against healthcare and critical illness risks.
Slavich said critical illness protection should complement medical insurance as part of a more comprehensive approach to financial security.
He said Allianz was also expanding its Discovery Health platform to support prevention, healthcare navigation and recovery.
The platform is intended to help customers access information on doctors, treatment and prevention programmes, while supporting them throughout their recovery journey.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Fall from 63cm can prove fatal - expert
Article:
BUTTERWORTH: A fall from as little as 63cm can result in serious injuries or even death, depending on how the victim lands and the surrounding conditions.
Universiti Utara Malaysia (UUM) Risk Management Division deputy director Dr Syazwan Syah Zulkifly said the severity of a fall could not be assessed based on height alone.
He said falls from lower levels often received less attention because workplace accidents were commonly associated with roofs, scaffolding, ladders or other elevated structures.
"Although the height may be low, the consequences can still be serious," he said when commenting on the case of a telecommunications tower maintenance worker who fell about 63cm at Kampung Juru, Simpang Ampat, on July 11.
The worker died 37 days later after receiving treatment at several hospitals.
Syazwan said an initial Department of Occupational Safety and Health (DOSH) chronology report stated that the tower area was overgrown with bushes and long grass, prompting the victim to allegedly walk on a plinth to avoid the affected route.
He said the incident raised broader questions about workplace environmental factors, rather than focusing solely on the worker's actions immediately before the fall.
"Safety management means assessing whether access routes, surfaces, equipment layout and handholds are safe and suitable for workers.
"Safety responsibility should not be placed solely on workers. Employers must ensure work systems, workplaces, access, equipment, information, instructions, training and supervision are in place to support safe work practices," he added.
Syazwan also stressed that risk assessments should not merely be compliance documents but must be translated into practical safety measures at the workplace.
He said working conditions could change and new hazards could emerge, requiring risk assessments to be reviewed whenever changes could affect the level of risk.
"A workplace that is safe today may be overgrown with bushes at another time. Surfaces can become slippery or uneven, while access routes can change and new hazards can emerge.
"In occupational safety, the question is not simply how high someone can fall, but whether the risk has been identified, assessed, communicated and controlled before an accident occurs," he said.
Syazwan also urged all parties not to speculate on the cause of the incident or assign blame while investigations were ongoing.
He said the tragedy should instead serve as a lesson to prevent similar incidents from recurring.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd
