Title: Dengue deaths rise to 12 in Johor as JB remains hotspot
Article:
JOHOR BARU: Twelve people have died from dengue in Johor so far this year, four more than the eight deaths recorded during the same period last year.
State Health and Environment Committee chairman Ling Tian Soon said Johor Baru remained the state's biggest hotspot, accounting for 492 cases, or 75.6 per cent, followed by Kulai with 115 cases.
State data showed 651 cases were reported during Epidemiological Week 33, a 3.4 per cent drop from 674 cases the previous week.
No new dengue deaths were reported during the week, but cumulative cases had surged 119.6 per cent to 9,290 as of Aug 23, from 4,231 during the corresponding period last year.
Fifty-nine new outbreak localities were detected during the week, with 44 in Johor Baru and 15 in Kulai.
The cumulative number of outbreak localities has now reached 1,001, up 123.9 per cent from 447 during the same period last year.
Ling said 341 of the 651 cases reported during the week came from outbreak localities, while 310 were from non-outbreak areas.
Ling said breeding sites were still being found inside and outside homes, indicating that residents remained insufficiently vigilant in eliminating stagnant water where Aedes mosquitoes could breed.
Enforcement teams have issued 3,694 compounds worth RM1.9 million this year, with 78.7 per cent already paid.
He urged residents to destroy mosquito breeding grounds, while schools were urged to conduct regular clean-up activities and school bus operators advised to use aerosol sprays inside buses before picking up and dropping off pupils.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: [UPDATED] Govt considering regulatory framework for e-commerce platforms
Article:
PUTRAJAYA: The Communications Ministry and Finance Ministry are exploring a regulatory framework for e-commerce platforms following public complaints about the safety standards and halal compliance of products sold online, Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said.
He said Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim issued the directive during the Cabinet meeting today to ensure consumers were adequately protected against misleading or substandard products.
"Views were raised regarding several e-commerce platforms that appear to be unregulated.
"There are concerns surrounding these platforms, whether regarding electrical and electronic equipment or the halal status of goods being sold.
"Thus, the prime minister has instructed the Finance Ministry and the Communications Ministry to look into immediate measures to implement regulatory processes, including registration requirements for e-commerce platforms," he said at a press conference here today.
Fahmi said the government aimed to ensure that all electrical and electronic goods sold online carried SIRIM certification, while food products strictly complied with local halal standards.
He added that authorities were also seeking to address issues surrounding foreign platforms that operate without local registration or a physical base in Malaysia.
According to data from the Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC), 1,964 complaints concerning e-commerce transactions, including online scam cases, have been recorded since Jan 1, 2025.
Of these, 1,147 complaints were lodged in 2025, while 817 have been received so far this year, with 118 cases currently being acted upon by the commission.
"A total of 191 complaints involved electrical and electronic goods, while four cases pertained to the authenticity of halal certifications," Fahmi said.
He added that the ministry would soon call e-commerce platforms for engagement sessions, drawing on its prior experience in implementing the licensing framework for social media platforms.
The need for regulatory oversight was also raised during the TikTok Shop Summit last week, which was attended by the Prime Minister.
At the summit, Anwar called for the drafting of the proposed
e-Commerce Bill
to be expedited to support the growth of the nation's digital economy.
Anwar said the legislation was aimed at improving the ease of doing business while strengthening regulatory oversight in line with the sector's rapid expansion.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Man sentenced to 30 years' jail, 12 strokes for murder
Article:
MUAR: A former mobile phone shop worker was jailed for 30 years and ordered to be caned 12 times by the High Court here today for killing a man with a metal object during a fight six years ago.
Judge Datuk Meor Hashimi Abdul Hamid handed down the sentence after finding Lim Yew Lung, 32, guilty of murdering Tsun Chin Kiang, 43.
The judge said the prosecution had proven all elements of the charge beyond reasonable doubt after considering the written and oral submissions by both sides.
He also found that the accused's defence, as well as those of two defence witnesses, failed to raise any reasonable doubt.
"The defence of the accused and the evidence of the second and third defence witnesses were not credible and could not be accepted by the court," he said.
Meor Hashimi ordered the 30-year sentence to run from the date of Lim's arrest on Jan 29, 2020.
The court also ordered all case exhibits to be handed over to police for disposal after the appeal period ends.
Deputy public prosecutor Othman Affan Ismail prosecuted, while Lim was represented by lawyer R. K. Balakrishnan.
Lim was charged with murdering Tsun at a mobile phone accessories shop in Jalan Perwira 1, Taman Perwira, between 1.41am and 4.15am on Jan 29, 2020.
He was initially charged under Section 302 of the Penal Code, which carried the mandatory death penalty upon conviction.
According to the facts of the case, a fight broke out between Lim and Tsun at the shop, leaving the victim seriously injured.
Tsun was rushed to Sultanah Aminah Hospital in Johor Baru but died four days later.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Public Bank Q2 net profit up 3.7pct, declares 10.5 sen dividend
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Public Bank Bhd's net profit rose 3.7 per cent to RM1.82 billion in the second quarter ended June 30, 2026, from RM1.76 billion a year earlier, as revenue increased 3.5 per cent to RM7.61 billion from RM7.35 billion.
In a bourse filing, Public Bank said the improved performance was mainly supported by higher non-interest income, which grew RM165.7 million, or 21.3 per cent, on stronger unit trust sales and higher unit trust management fee income.
The gains were partly offset by an RM81.1 million increase in impairment allowances on loans and financing, reflecting the normalisation of credit charges, as well as a RM26.3 million, or two per cent, rise in other operating expenses.
Public Bank declared a first interim dividend of 10.5 sen per share for the financial year ending Dec 31, 2026, involving a total payout of RM2.04 billion.
For the first half of 2026, net profit increased 2.02 per cent to RM3.58 billion from RM3.51 billion a year earlier, while revenue rose 1.7 per cent to RM14.93 billion from RM14.67 billion.
On its outlook, Public Bank said ongoing geopolitical tensions, volatility in global financial markets, trade tariffs and persistent fiscal imbalances were expected to weigh on global growth.
Despite the uncertainties, it said Malaysia's banking sector remained resilient, supported by ample liquidity and strong capital buffers.
"Public Bank will continue to uphold its commitment to further strengthen its role as a financial intermediary in support of national development.
"The group will continue to prioritise prudence in the management of credit risk, uphold strong corporate governance and effective risk management practices to safeguard stakeholder value," it said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Lynas expands global footprint, eyes new rare earths supply deals
Article:
MELBOURNE: Australia's Lynas Rare Earths said it planned to grow its global supply chain on Wednesday, with discussions to secure new mine supply from project developers around the world and set up a magnet processing facility in the United States.
The comments came after the world's biggest producer of rare earths outside China reported a sharp rise in annual profit, helped by record average selling prices for rare-earth oxide and strong demand, but missed market expectations. Its shares fell as much as eight per cent.
Interim chief executive officer (CEO) Pol Le Roux said Lynas is in talks with project developers of ionic clay deposits around the world for new supply and expects to announce new deals soon. He did not say whether that would involve buying material or acquiring ionic clay businesses.
"I think they held the door ajar and they're considering all of that," said Barrenjoey analyst Daniel Morgan.
Le Roux also said Lynas was in early-stage talks with various parties to develop a magnet-making facility in the US.
"But we are on track on that development and more development is to come," he said on an earnings call.
The US, Europe and their allies are racing to build supply chains to reduce their dependence on China, which accounts for some 90 per cent of global production of rare earth products, including magnets used in the aerospace, automotive and defence industries.
A one-year suspension on export controls announced by China on several medium and heavy rare earth products expires in November.
SOARING PROFIT MISSES FORECASTS
Lynas posted a net profit after tax of A$222.4 million (US$159.37 million) for the year ended June 30, up from A$8 million a year ago. That missed a Visible Alpha consensus estimate of A$242.5 million.
It flagged operational challenges tied to ore quality at its Mt Weld mine in Australia, as well as rising costs. However it said it has resolved quality issues at its Kalgoorlie plant.
"They have fixed a whole bunch of problems. It's nice to know they have found better operational stability," Morgan added.
The earnings surge was driven by firm prices and floor price agreements with both Japanese and US customers, which helped reduce volatility, Lynas said.
Its average selling price rose 59 per cent to A$80.7 per kilogram, helped by improved pricing of neodymium-praseodymium, a key rare-earth magnet material, and a higher share of heavy rare-earth sales and sales with pricing not linked to the market index.
Customers continued to prioritise sustainable rare-earth supply chains outside China amid export restrictions, while strong demand lifted sales volumes, it said.
The company is searching for a new CEO, following the retirement of Amanda Lacaze.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: [UPDATED] Govt to decide today on National Day celebrations amid haze
Article:
PUTRAJAYA: The government will decide whether to adjust the scale and venue of the 2026 National Day celebrations amid deteriorating air quality caused by haze nationwide, says Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil.
He said Chief Secretary to the Government Tan Sri Shamsul Azri Abu Bakar would make the decision following discussions with the Communications Ministry, Natural Resources and Environmental Sustainability Ministry, Malaysian Meteorological Department, Education Ministry and Health Ministry.
"The Chief Secretary to the Government will hold discussions and subsequently make a decision regarding the scale, venue and necessary measures to be undertaken by organisers to ensure the health and safety of not only visitors and spectators, but also participants.
"They will evaluate and review the situation and make a decision based on weather projections for the next five to six days, taking into account possible scenarios, including haze.
"A decision will be reached today," he said at a press conference here today.
The National Day parade is scheduled to be held at Dataran Putrajaya on Aug 31, subject to the government's decision.
The government will also assess the National Day Eve programme on Aug 30 at Dataran Merdeka, jointly organised by Kuala Lumpur City Hall (DBKL) and CIMB.
Fahmi said the health and safety of 1,500 secondary school students from three states taking part in the human graphic performance would be considered in the final decision.
Yesterday,
30 areas nationwide recorded unhealthy
Air Pollutant Index (API) readings, with Putrajaya logging a level of 155.
As of 3pm today, air quality in Putrajaya remained at an unhealthy 155, even as the total number of areas registering unhealthy air levels nationwide dropped to 10.
An API reading between 0 and 50 is categorised as good, 51 to 100 as moderate, 101 to 200 as unhealthy, 201 to 300 as very unhealthy, and 300 and above as hazardous.
MetMalaysia director-general Dr Mohd Hisham Mohd Anip previously said the
haze affecting several parts of the country
was unlikely to clear until open burning in neighbouring countries was brought under control.
He said the current hot and dry spell was expected to continue over the next few days.
Prevailing winds from
Kalimantan and Sumatra were carrying transboundary haze
directly into Sarawak and the west coast of Peninsular Malaysia.
Malaysia has expressed readiness
to assist Indonesia in efforts
to put out forest and peatland fires.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Father, 9-year-old son found dead hugging in house fire
Article:
KUALA NERUS: A man and his nine-year-old son were found dead in an embrace after they were trapped in a house fire at Kampung Tok Jembal, here.
The victims were identified as Amirulfahmi Wan Jusoh, 40, and his son, Rehan Yusuf, 9.
The fire broke out at about 4am, with the pair found on the upper floor of the two-storey house.
The victims' brother-in-law, Nik Mohd Zaim Nik Abdul Rahim, 36, said his mother-in-law, Maimunah Muda, 67, who was sleeping on the ground floor, was rescued by a family member who lived in the neighbouring house.
He said Amirulfahmi, the fourth of eight siblings, worked in advertising, specialising in photography and videography, at a restaurant in Kuala Terengganu.
"Amirulfahmi, who was fondly known as Uda, returned to his mother's house with Rehan yesterday.
[[nid:1519189]]
"Before that, he was at his in-laws' house in Kampung Paloh, Kuala Terengganu, to visit his wife, Nur Izzah Ahmad, who is in her 30s and had just completed her confinement period.
"The deceased and his son then returned to his mother's house. They were reportedly in the process of moving here to care for their mother (Maimunah), who was unwell," he said when met at the scene.
Meanwhile, witness Wan Azrin Wan Awang, 46, said he rushed to the house after hearing his wife scream that a fire had broken out.
"My wife shouted that a house was on fire. I immediately ran there. When I arrived, two villagers were already at the scene.
"We tried calling out to the occupants and knocked on the main door, but there was no response.
"We then had to kick down the door, which was locked from inside, before one of the occupants' children, who lived next door, entered the house to retrieve a motorcycle and pull the woman out," he said.
Wan Azrin said they were then informed that two more victims, the woman's son and grandson, were still upstairs.
"We called out to them repeatedly, but there was no response. At the same time, the fire grew more intense and began spreading through the house," he said.
He said he did not hear anything unusual before realising the house was on fire.
"I did not hear any sound before that. Everything happened in a chaotic situation, and I heard what sounded like an explosion, like the roof burning," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Bandar Utama school murder trial: Defence closes case after boy testifies
Article:
SHAH ALAM, Aug 26 — The defence in the case of a 15-year-old boy charged with murdering a female student at a secondary school in Bandar Utama, Petaling Jaya, last year closed its case today after all defence witnesses had completed their testimony.
Judge Adlin Abdul Majid directed the prosecution and defence to file their respective replies on Sept 3, with oral submissions scheduled for Sept 8.
Speaking to reporters outside the court, defence lawyer Kitson Foong said the defence had completed its case after two witnesses, including the accused, testified.
“Besides the accused, the other witness called to testify was Hospital Bahagia Ulu Kinta Consultant Forensic Psychiatrist Dr Ian Lloyd Anthony,” he said.
The teenager is charged with murdering the victim, who was 16 at the time, in a girls’ toilet at a secondary school in Bandar Utama between 9.20 am and 9.35 am on Oct 14, 2025.
The charge was framed under Section 302 of the Penal Code, which carries the death penalty, although the accused, being a juvenile, is subject to the provisions of the Child Act 2001.
The prosecution is led by Deputy Public Prosecutors Raja Zaizul Faridah Raja Zaharudin, Aqharie Durranie Aziz and Ahmad Iqbal Azman.
As the accused is a minor, his identity cannot be disclosed or his photograph taken, while the entire proceedings were conducted in camera.
On Feb 12, the teenager pleaded not guilty after the charge was read out again in Mandarin before Judge Adlin.
On Jan 30, the prosecution obtained the Attorney General’s consent under Section 177A of the Criminal Procedure Code to transfer the case from the Petaling Jaya Magistrate’s Court to the Shah Alam High Court for trial after a psychiatric report found the teenager fit to stand trial.
On Oct 22, 2025, the teenager was charged in the Petaling Jaya Magistrate’s Court, but no plea was recorded as murder cases fall under the jurisdiction of the High Court.
Section 97(1) of the Child Act 2001 provides that the death penalty cannot be imposed on an offender below 18 years of age upon conviction.
Instead, the court may order the offender to be detained for such period as determined by the Yang di-Pertuan Agong, the Ruler or Yang Dipertua Negeri, under Section 97(2) of the same Act. — Bernama

Title: Ismail Sabri set to face charge over asset declaration tomorrow
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 26 — Former Prime Minister Datuk Seri Ismail Sabri Yaakob will be charged at the Kuala Lumpur Sessions Court tomorrow under the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) Act.
Lawyer Datuk Amer Hamzah Arshad, who represents Ismail Sabri, 66, confirmed to Bernama today that his client would appear in court tomorrow.
A check of the court system showed that the case would be mentioned before Judge Suzana Hussin at 9 am.
The Bera MP is expected to face charges under Section 36(2) of the MACC Act 2009 relating to the declaration of assets.
Ismail Sabri was initially scheduled to be charged on Aug 7, but the proceedings were postponed to Aug 27 after he was admitted to the National Heart Institute (IJN) due to health issues.
Judge Suzana then postponed the case to Aug 27 after Amer Hamzah sought an adjournment, saying Ismail Sabri was experiencing possible arrhythmia and was scheduled to undergo a pacemaker procedure.
Amer Hamzah said his client experienced a heart problem while having his statement recorded by MACC on Aug 6.
The former prime minister had previously been called several times to have his statement recorded regarding the asset declaration made to MACC.
MACC also seized RM170 million in cash in various foreign currencies and confiscated 16 kilogrammes of pure gold bars, estimated to be worth RM7 million, as part of an investigation into alleged corruption and money laundering involving the former prime minister.
The seizures were made during searches of a residence and an office allegedly used as ‘safe houses’, following investigations into four of Ismail Sabri’s senior officers who were detained in February last year. — Bernama

Title: Heartbreak and hope as injured elephant ‘Sulong’ treks 100km back to Gua Musang
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 26 — An injured wild male elephant has captured national attention after embarking on a journey across the Titiwangsa Range along the East-West Highway (JRTB) to return to his home habitat in Gua Musang, Kelantan, just days after being relocated to Gerik, Perak.
Affectionately named Sulong Chalil, the elephant has drawn widespread sympathy across social media as he treks eastward along the highway shoulder despite nursing an injury to his right front leg.
The Department of Wildlife and National Parks (Perhilitan) confirmed that rangers are closely monitoring the animal's welfare and movements. Perhilitan said Sulong remains in stable condition, displaying normal behaviour, feeding regularly, and moving steadily.
Perhilitan added that the wound on his right leg is drying and showing positive signs of recovery. To prevent untoward incidents and ensure road safety, Perhilitan Perak teams are deployed twice daily, during both daytime and night hours, to track the animal and herd him safely away from oncoming expressway traffic.
The elephant’s story went viral after social media user Mohd Fadli Salleh shared details regarding his background, explaining that the name Chalil originated from the village in Gua Musang where the elephant previously roamed before being captured.
“Stories about this elephant have been circulating since yesterday. It turns out many people do not know the real story of this elephant.
“Some time ago, residents in Gua Musang lodged complaints because a herd of elephants had entered plantations and posed a danger to residents.
“The Department of Wildlife and National Parks (Perhilitan) went to Gua Musang, captured Sulong and then relocated him to the forest in Gerik, Perak,” he wrote.
However, several days after his release into the Gerik jungle, Sulong reappeared on Aug 17 along the Gerik-Jeli route, steadily walking in the direction of Kelantan. Motorists who encountered him noted that the animal did not display any aggressive behaviour.
“Sulong is believed to be homesick and missing his original home. Guided by his instincts, he has been walking for days.
“Now Sulong is near Jeli, having walked more than 100 kilometres through the Titiwangsa Range to return to his original home,” Fadli added.
Images of the limping elephant has triggered an outpouring of support and prayers online.
“Go Sulong go! Just a little more to go. May Sulong successfully reach his hometown and live in peace and harmony,” wrote one Facebook user.
Another commenter posted: “My heart hurts seeing the wound on your leg. May Allah protect your welfare, Sulong Chalil, and may you arrive safely.”
A separate update shared on social media noted encouraging signs in his recovery.

Title: ‘If Muhyiddin did not help me… I would not donate RM4.8m to PPBM’, Bumi contractor says in Jana Wibawa trial
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 26 — A Bumiputera businessman who secured a RM62 million government project under the Jana Wibawa programme told the High Court today that Tan Sri Muhyiddin Yassin had in 2020 said contractors could donate directly to his political party Parti Pribumi Bersatu Malaysia (PPBM).
Datuk Seri Azman Yusoff, 54, president of the Bumiputera Contractors Association of Malaysia (PKBM) and managing director of Bumiputera-owned KCJ Engineering Sdn Bhd, was testifying as the 27th prosecution witness in Muhyiddin’s power abuse and money laundering trial.
Having known Muhyiddin since 2016, when he was deputy prime minister, Azman said he had in July 2020 joined the Tan Sri Muhyiddin Charity Golf (TSMCG) tournament at the Tropicana Golf Club when the politician was prime minister and president of PPBM, which is also called Bersatu.
After the tournament, Azman said he had met Muhyiddin alone at 3pm in a room at the golf club to ask about opportunities for government projects for PKBM members, and that he had never heard about the Jana Wibawa programme before the then-PM told him about it in that meeting.
“Also in that meeting, Tan Sri Muhyiddin said spontaneously to me, if there are any PKBM members or contractors who wish to donate, can donate directly to Parti Pribumi Bersatu Malaysia and not to any individuals in PPBM,” Azman said.
Azman said that was why he had asked contractors whom he had met and who wished to apply for Jana Wibawa projects to donate directly to Bersatu.
Recalling the conversation in which he had asked about Jana Wibawa projects via direct negotiation, Azman said he believed he had to comply with Muhyiddin’s donation request.
“I considered that notification as a sentence that means that Tan Sri Muhyiddin Yassin hopes there would be donations from companies which get projects under Jana Wibawa to PPBM as he had previously mentioned donations during that conversation.
“So I as a businessman who wished to request for support and help from him considered that notification as having to be complied with,” he said to explain why he eventually donated RM4.8 million to Bersatu.
After being told by Muhyiddin to get further information from his deputy chief private secretary Asmar Asmadi Abdullah Sani, Azman said he had met the aide several days later in Parliament and was shown a list of around 10 approved government projects under Jana Wibawa.
Jana Wibawa was meant to help Bumiputera contractors with Grade G7 status through appointments as government contractors through direct negotiations.
Azman said he had asked how to apply for these projects, and that Asmar Asmadi had said application letters to Muhyiddin, together with company profiles, could be sent to him.
Azman said he had signed KCJ’s September 21, 2020 letter addressed to Muhyiddin and handed it to Asmar Asmadi at the Prime Minister’s Office (PMO).
In the letter, KCJ asked for Muhyiddin’s support in its application to be appointed via direct negotiation as the contractor for a Jana Wibawa project to build a new road from Felda Bukit Jalur to Gemas, Negeri Sembilan, with the company stating it was a fully owned Bumiputera contractor with Grade G7 status.
The Public Works Department (PWD), in a March 23, 2021 letter, informed KCJ that the government had decided to procure the project via direct negotiation with the company, and in a May 27, 2021 letter asked the company to provide its tender documents for the project.
After providing its tender and offer price, KCJ Engineering was awarded the RM62 million project on July 30, 2021.
After being awarded the project, Azman said he had met and informed Bersatu treasurer Datuk Mohamed Salleh Bajuri that his company planned to donate around five per cent of the RM62 million project to Bersatu.
Ultimately, Azman and his company KCJ Engineering donated RM4.8 million, or around seven to eight per cent of the RM62 million project, as he knew from experience that the profits from building government roads could be around 15 to 20 per cent.
To donate to Bersatu, Azman said he had borrowed RM4 million from his company KCJ Engineering, which he said would be repaid by the company’s year-end dividend payments to him as managing director.
Using the borrowed RM4 million, Azman confirmed he had signed two CIMB cheques on September 7, 2021 for RM2 million and RM1 million, and two November 1, 2022 CIMB cheques for RM500,000 each, and hand-delivered them to Salleh.
Azman said he had delivered KCJ Engineering’s four Maybank Islamic cheques dated September 1, 2022, totalling RM800,000, to Salleh.
Azman said he did not receive any receipt from Bersatu for the RM4.8 million donation.
Previously, bank documents in this trial had shown that the RM4 million from Azman and RM800,000 from KCJ had entered Bersatu’s CIMB account.
Azman said he had paid the RM4.8 million in advance although his company had yet to receive any payments from the government for the project, as he knew the payments would come later since his company had been awarded the project and he recalled Muhyiddin’s July 2020 remarks.
Acknowledging that he did have the choice not to donate to Bersatu, Azman said he had still donated because, as a businessman, he had to comply with Muhyiddin’s July 2020 request.
Although Muhyiddin was no longer prime minister at that time, Azman said he and KCJ had still paid RM4.8 million to Bersatu in 2021 and 2022 “because I as a businessman wished to ‘membalas budi’ (repay the deeds)” of Muhyiddin’s help in getting the project through direct negotiation, and also because he remembered Muhyiddin’s July 2020 remarks.
Azman said he and KCJ would not have donated RM4.8 million to Bersatu if Muhyiddin did not “spontaneously” tell him that any contractors who wished to donate could donate directly to Bersatu.
“If Tan Sri Muhyiddin Yassin did not help me to get this project through direct negotiation, I would not donate RM4.8 million to PPBM,” he said.
Azman said he believed his company would not have secured the project through direct negotiation if its application letter had not been supported by Muhyiddin and processed by the PMO, adding that Muhyiddin’s support was an advantage as his company did not have to compete with other companies via a tender.
Azman, who was Umno Lembah Pantai division committee member from 2013 to 2018, said he and his company had never donated to other political parties besides PPBM.
Referring to this project, which his company was awarded through direct negotiation, Azman said: “I did not make any donations to any other political parties as I am only ‘terhutang budi’ (indebted) to Tan Sri Muhyiddin Yassin who has helped me and KCJ Engineering.”
With 25 years of experience in handling government projects in the construction industry, Azman said he believed that a prime minister can help influence the actions and decisions of any ministers in the Malaysian government, as the PM is head of government and has the power to appoint and fire any ministers.
As for a separate Jana Wibawa project to build a road from Kampung Gong Nangka to Bukit Khor, Marang, Terengganu, worth RM29.8 million, Azman said he did not donate to Bersatu as his company had won the project while competing with other unknown companies through a pre-qualification tender and without getting Muhyiddin’s help.
In this trial, Muhyiddin is facing seven charges, namely four counts of alleged power abuse to obtain RM225.3 million in bribes for his party, Bersatu (from Nepturis Sdn Bhd, Azman Yusoff, KCJ Engineering Sdn Bhd, Bukhary Equity Sdn Bhd and Mamfor Sdn Bhd), and three counts of alleged money laundering involving money that Bersatu received from Bukhary Equity.
The trial before High Court judge Noor Ruwena Md Nurdin resumes tomorrow.

Title: Muhyiddin’s request for Bersatu donations was wrong, Bumiputera contractor chief tells court
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 26 — Then prime minister Tan Sri Muhyiddin Yassin’s July 2020 request for contractors to make donations to his political party Parti Pribumi Bersatu Malaysia during a conversation about government projects for Bumiputera contractors was wrong, a witness told the High Court today.
Bumiputera Contractors Association of Malaysia (PKBM) president Datuk Seri Azman Yusoff said this as the prosecution’s 27th witness in Muhyiddin’s power abuse and money laundering trial.
Despite acknowledging that Muhyiddin’s request was wrong, Azman also expressed gratitude to him for helping Bumiputera contractors via government projects under the Jana Wibawa programme during the Covid-19 pandemic, and said he had no malicious motives against the politician.
Today, Azman said Muhyiddin had “spontaneously” told him during their one-on-one July 2020 meeting at the Tropicana Golf Club that contractors who wished to donate could donate directly to Bersatu instead of to individuals in the party.
Azman said Muhyiddin had spoken about the donations “spontaneously” when he was asking the then Prime Minister about opportunities for government projects for Bumiputera contractors under his association, and that Muhyiddin had also informed him about the Jana Wibawa programme in this meeting.
Asked by lead prosecutor Datuk Wan Shaharuddin Wan Ladin if he knew it was wrong for Muhyiddin to make the donation request, Azman agreed that it was wrong.
“Yes, I certainly agree this is an offence, but I as a businessman, I have to agree with the prime minister for the continuity of my business and also my friends’ businesses.
“At that time, everything was paralysed because no projects were going on. Thank God with Tan Sri Muhyiddin Yassin’s help, we were awarded projects. With that, I agree with the payment informed by Tan Sri Muhyiddin Yassin for donations to be given to the party Bersatu. He informed spontaneously to me and also to other contractors,” he said.
Asked by Wan Shaharuddin if he had any malice against Muhyiddin when testifying against him in this trial while also being indebted to the politician, Azman said he had no malicious intent.
Noting that there were no construction projects that could be carried out during the Covid-19 pandemic, Azman went on to thank Muhyiddin: “So thank you to Tan Sri Muhyiddin Yassin for helping Bumiputera contractors during Covid-19.”
After Muhyiddin’s July 2020 donation remarks, Azman said his Bumiputera construction company KCJ Engineering Sdn Bhd which had a Grade G7 contractor status later applied for a government project under Jana Wibawa through a written request for Muhyiddin’s support.
He said Jana Wibawa was meant to help Bumiputera contractors with Grade G7 status through appointments as government contractors through direct negotiations.
Azman said he had handed over KCJ Engineering’s September 21, 2020 project application letter to Muhyiddin’s aide at the Prime Minister’s Office, with the letter addressed to Muhyiddin and seeking his support for the company to be appointed for the project through direct negotiation.
After KCJ Engineering was awarded the RM62 million government project on July 30, 2021, Azman said he and his company had together issued eight cheques totalling RM4.8 million as donations to Bersatu (with RM4 million issued from his personal account and RM800,000 from the company’s account).
Segambut Bersatu division deputy chief Adam Radlan Adam Muhammad is seen at the Kuala Lumpur Court Complex on February 16, 2024. — Picture by Sayuti Zainudin
Azman said the RM4.8 million donation was because of Muhyiddin’s July 2020 remarks and as he wanted to repay Muhyiddin’s kind deeds in helping him get the project through direct negotiation, noting that RM4.8 million was around seven to eight per cent of the contract’s RM62 million value.
Because of Muhyiddin’s “spontaneous” July 2020 remarks about donations, Azman said he had also asked Nepturis Sdn Bhd’s representative Lian Tan Chuan and Sutracom Sdn Bhd’s representative Shahradzi Shamsuddin to donate to Bersatu after the two Bumiputera companies were awarded Jana Wibawa projects.
Shahradzi previously told the court that his company Mamfor Sdn Bhd had donated RM19.5 million to Bersatu as his younger brother’s company Sutracom was awarded a RM605.2 million project, while Lian had confirmed a RM1 million cheque to Bersatu after Nepturis was given a RM141 million project.
Among other things, Azman said he had first known Segambut Bersatu division deputy chief Adam Radlan Adam Muhammad during the Tan Sri Muhyiddin Charity Golf tournament in July 2020 and found out that the latter was close to Muhyiddin due to his Bersatu position.
Azman said he had introduced Lian to Adam Radlan in a December 2020 meeting at Publika, Kuala Lumpur attended by the trio, adding that Adam Radlan had confirmed he had a close relationship with Muhyiddin and could help Lian’s company get Jana Wibawa projects.
Azman said he later asked Lian to donate RM1 million to Bersatu, as he believed that Lian’s company had obtained the Jana Wibawa project as it was supported by Muhyiddin after the company’s letter expressing interest in the project was forwarded by Adam Radlan to the PM.
“Besides that, because I remember Tan Sri Muhyiddin Yassin himself informing me previously that any companies which obtain Jana Wibawa projects can make donations directly to Bersatu,” he said.
Azman said Lian in 2022 handed him a RM1 million cheque for Bersatu, and that he then gave the cheque to Bersatu’s treasurer Datuk Mohamed Salleh Bajuri.
Azman said there are around 300 Bumiputera contractors with the Grade G7 status in his association PKBM.
Azman’s association PKBM was formed in 2018, and he has been the president since then.
Azman is also president of PPIPBM, an association for Malaysia’s Bumiputera manufacturers and service industry players, and is also currently a director in the Construction Industry Development Board (CIDB).
In this trial, Muhyiddin is facing seven charges, namely four counts of alleged power abuse to obtain RM225.3 million in bribes for his party, Parti Pribumi Bersatu Malaysia (from Nepturis Sdn Bhd, Datuk Seri Azman Yusoff, KCJ Engineering Sdn Bhd, Bukhary Equity Sdn Bhd and Mamfor Sdn Bhd), and three counts of alleged money laundering involving money that Bersatu received from Bukhary Equity.
The trial before High Court judge Noor Ruwena Md Nurdin resumes tomorrow, with Muhyiddin’s lawyers expected to cross-examine Azman.
