Title: Preacher, NGO secretary claim trial to RM13.8m CBT and money laundering charges
Article:
SEREMBAN, Aug 26 — A 40-year-old “religious influencer” claimed trial at the Sessions Court here today to 34 charges of criminal breach of trust (CBT) involving more than RM13.8 million belonging to a non-governmental organisation.
Abdullah Abdol Razak, an independent preacher who served as chairman of Pertubuhan Rezeki Infaq Malaysia during the alleged offences, also pleaded not guilty before judge Kunasundary Marimuthu to 17 separate money laundering charges involving RM1.55 million,
The Star
reported.
The CBT offences were allegedly committed at a commercial bank in Seremban 2 between February 2023 and March 2026, while the money laundering offences allegedly took place at the same location between May 2024 and February 2026.
The CBT charges, framed under Section 409 of the Penal Code, provide for a prison sentence of between two and 20 years, whipping, and a fine upon conviction.
The money laundering charges under Section 4(1)(b) of the Anti-Money Laundering, Anti-Terrorism Financing and Proceeds of Unlawful Activities Act 2001 (AMLA) carry a jail term of up to 15 years and a fine of not less than five times the sum of the illicit proceeds or RM5 million, whichever is higher.
The NGO’s secretary, 30-year-old Noor Sahira Abdullah, was separately charged with abetment under Section 109 of the Penal Code, read together with Section 409. She claimed trial to all counts.
Pertubuhan Rezeki Infaq Malaysia (PRIM) secretary Noor Sahira Abdullah pleads not guilty at the Seremban Session Court to 34 counts of abetting the organization’s chairman Abdullah Abdol Razak by intentionally helping him transfer money via online banking in Seremban on August 26, 2026. — Bernama pic
Deputy Public Prosecutor Datuk Ahmad Akram Gharib informed the court that while the offences were non-bailable, the prosecution would offer bail at RM1 million with two sureties for Abdullah, subject to additional conditions that he surrender his passport and refrain from tampering with prosecution witnesses.
Lead defence counsel Azrul Zulkifli Stork pleaded for a lower bail amount, arguing that the accused’s bank accounts had been frozen and that Abdullah, who runs a restaurant, needs to support his 11 children, wife, and elderly mother.
Kunasundary granted bail at RM700,000, comprising RM300,000 in unsecured bail with two sureties, while allowing the prosecution’s application for passport surrender and witness non-interference.
For Noor Sahira, Deputy Public Prosecutor Syairah Aqilah Khalil proposed bail at RM250,000 with two sureties. Azruul appealed for a reduction, saying that she earns RM3,000 monthly and supports her five-month-old infant and parents. The court subsequently set her bail at RM200,000 with two sureties.
Both cases have been fixed for mention on Sept 28.

Title: No shutdown, but Fahmi says e-commerce platforms to face tighter rules over electrical, halal products
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Aug 26 — The government will take immediate steps to tighten oversight of e-commerce platforms following complaints over products sold online, Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said today.
He said Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim had directed the Finance Ministry and Communications Ministry to examine regulatory measures after receiving complaints from members of the public, e-commerce operators and traders with physical shops.
“There were views expressed regarding several e-commerce platforms which appeared to be insufficiently regulated. These platforms either have issues involving the products being sold, particularly electrical and electronic equipment, or the halal status of products being offered.
“The prime minister has therefore instructed the Ministry of Finance and the Ministry of Communications to examine immediate measures to implement regulatory processes, including registration requirements for e-commerce platforms,” Fahmi said during his weekly post-Cabinet press conference here.
He said some platforms had companies registered and based in Malaysia, while others did not have a locally registered company or address.
Fahmi said the government had no intention of shutting down the platforms but wanted products sold online to comply with Malaysian standards.
“For example, electrical and electronic products must comply with Sirim standards, while products carrying halal status must comply with the halal standards adopted in the country,” he said.
The Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC) received 1,964 complaints involving e-commerce platforms and related matters, including scams, from January 1, 2025 to August 25 this year.
Of these, 1,147 complaints were received last year and 817 between January 1 and August 25 this year, with 118 cases still under action by the MCMC.
Fahmi said 161 complaints involved electrical or electronic products, while four concerned the validity of halal status of products sold online.
He said the MCMC would engage e-commerce platforms, drawing on its experience in regulating social media platforms.
“We will invite these platforms to engage in discussions and consultation sessions.
“For the MCMC, the licensing framework previously used for social media platforms has given the MCMC experience in terms of what needs to be done when engaging with platforms. Therefore, similar discussions could perhaps be held with the e-commerce platforms,” he said.

Title: Thick haze forces rethink of National Day celebrations in Putrajaya, but cancellation not on cards
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Aug 26 — The government is reviewing the scale and location of this year’s National Day celebrations amid the haze affecting several parts of the country, but cancellation is not being considered at this stage, Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said today.
He said the Cabinet had been briefed by the Malaysian Meteorological Department on the haze situation, including in Putrajaya and Kuala Lumpur, as well as Sarawak, which has been significantly affected.
“We will not cancel the event, but the scale may be changed or the location may be changed,” Fahmi said in his weekly post-Cabinet press conference here.
He said Chief Secretary to the Government Tan Sri Shamsul Azri Abu Bakar would chair a meeting this afternoon with relevant agencies to assess the situation and determine the appropriate measures for the celebrations.
The meeting will involve the Communications Ministry, Natural Resources and Environmental Sustainability Ministry, Meteorological Department, Education Ministry and Health Ministry, among other agencies.
Fahmi said the government would assess weather forecasts and projections for the next five to six days, including the expected haze conditions, before making a decision.
The review will cover the National Day celebrations scheduled for August 31 at Dataran Putrajaya, as well as the National Day Eve programme on August 30 at Dataran Merdeka, organised by Kuala Lumpur City Hall and banking giant CIMB.
He said the decision would take into account the safety and health of both visitors and participants.
Fahmi added that the Education and Health Ministries would also be consulted as the National Day celebrations involve about 1,500 secondary school students from three states participating in the human graphic formation.
The final decision on the events is expected to be made following the meeting chaired by Shamsul later today.
Yesterday, Putrajaya recorded 156 in the Air Pollutant Index (API).
Under national environmental standards, an API reading between 101 and 200 is officially classified as “Unhealthy”.

Title: Bersatu Youth chief hints at possible cooperation with Selangor government
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 26 — Bersatu Youth chief Hilman Idham has suggested that his party could back Pakatan Harapan in the Selangor government until the end of its current term.
The Gombak Setia assemblyman was responding to the recent move by two Bersatu representatives in Pahang who pledged support for Barisan Nasional Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Wan Rosdy Wan Ismail.
Asked whether a similar political arrangement could take shape in Selangor, Hilman said it was “not impossible”, Malaysiakini reported.
“Bersatu has worked with all political parties before, including BN and Harapan. The fundamental consideration is the people’s interests,” he said.
His remarks arrive amid mounting talk of potential realignments in Selangor ahead of the next state election.
Earlier this month, Selangor Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Amirudin Shari said that PH remained open to working with any party, including Bersatu and Perikatan Nasional, provided it ensures political stability and benefits the public.
Amirudin noted, however, that no formal or serious discussions had taken place between PH and Bersatu in the state.
Former Selangor MB and current Hulu Kelang assemblyman Datuk Seri Azmin Ali, who heads Selangor PN, currently leads Bersatu in the state assembly.
Azmin is a former PKR leader who left the party as part of the so-called Sheraton Move, with Hilman following suit shortly after.
Speculation over cross-party cooperation has gathered pace following recent developments in Pahang, where Bersatu’s sole two assemblymen, Jasri Jamaludin (Kuala Sentul) and Yazid Yunus (Lepar), crossed the aisle to back Wan Rosdy.
In Melaka, Bersatu has also expressed readiness to explore talks with parties sharing common ground, including PH, as it assesses potential electoral arrangements.
Hilman suggested that the political thaw in Pahang could pave the way for similar pacts elsewhere.
“Politically, Harapan may not need Bersatu. But if it happens, perhaps a convergence of ideas and thinking could strengthen programmes and initiatives for the people of Selangor,” he said.
PH controls 32 of the 56 seats in the Selangor legislative assembly, while BN holds two.
Bersatu occupies 11 seats and PAS holds 10, with former Bersatu representative Abdul Rashid Asari sitting as an independent aligned with Amirudin’s administration.

Title: Kluang used car dealer claims trial over illegal possession of Smith & Wesson pistol
Article:
KLUANG, Aug 26 — A used car dealer pleaded not guilty at the Sessions Court here today to a charge of possessing a firearm without a valid licence earlier this month.
How Han Wei, 33, entered the plea after the charge was read out to him before Judge Hanie Dzatul Akhmar Zulkefli.
According to the charge sheet, How was alleged to have been in possession of a Smith & Wesson pistol without lawful authorisation at a house in Jalan Indah 2/10, Taman Kluang Indah, at about 6.30 pm on Aug 6.
He was charged under Section 8 of the Firearms (Increased Penalties) Act 1971, which carries a maximum jail term of 14 years and not less than six strokes of the cane upon conviction.
The prosecution was conducted by deputy public prosecutor Siti Nurfara Fazilun Izylin Ahmad, while How was represented by lawyer Yvonne Kee.
No bail was granted as the offence is non-bailable. The court fixed Sept 28 for mention of the case for the submission of documents.
How, together with three other men, was previously charged at the Batu Pahat Magistrate’s Court on Aug 17 with murdering a businessman earlier this month.
Earlier this month, How was among five suspects arrested after a 39-year-old man’s body was found floating in Sungai Tanjung Sembrong, Parit Raja.
Initial investigations found that the victim was believed to have been strangled with a rope before being taken in a vehicle, with his hands tied using adhesive tape and his body wrapped in a net.
The victim was reported missing by his wife on July 29, while his family only found his vehicle in Johor Bahru. — Bernama

Title: George Town roads to close for National Day parade from Aug 29–31: Here’s where
Article:
GEORGE TOWN, Aug 26 — Several major roads here will be closed from Aug 29 to 31 to facilitate the rehearsal and state-level 69th National Day Parade and celebrations at Jalan Padang Kota.
The Penang Island City Council (MBPP), in a statement today, said the road closures would begin at 2 am on Aug 29 and continue until 1 pm on Aug 31, or until the event concludes, covering several locations in the city centre.
“The roads affected include the Chulia Street Ghaut/Weld Quay junction, part of China Street Ghaut, Church Street, the Union Street/Beach Street junction and part of Penang Street from Light Street to Union Street.
“Also affected are part of King Street from Bishop Street to Light Street, the Light Street/Kapitan Keling Mosque Road junction and the Tun Syed Sheh Barakbah Road/Light Street junction,” it said.
MBPP advised motorists to plan their journeys, follow instructions from personnel at the affected locations and use alternative routes to avoid traffic congestion. — Bernama

Title: Penang tycoon Tan Kok Ping loses libel appeal against CM Chow Kon Yeow, ordered to pay RM50,000
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Aug 26 — The Court of Appeal here today upheld the High Court’s dismissal of businessman Tan Sri Tan Kok Ping’s libel suit against Penang Chief Minister Chow Kon Yeow.
A three-member bench comprising Justices Datuk Dr Alwi Abdul Wahab, Datuk Dr Shahnaz Sulaiman and Datuk Amarjeet Singh unanimously dismissed Tan’s appeal against the Nov 26, 2024 High Court decision.
Delivering the court’s decision, Justice Alwi said that the High Court did not commit any error which warranted appellate intervention.
“The respondent’s (Chow’s) statements could be regarded as fair comment as they constituted an honest opinion based on proven facts concerning a matter of public interest, namely the governance of a charitable institution,” he said.
He said Chow’s defence of justification had been established because the substance of the statements was generally true, and the doctrine of “half-truth” did not apply as no material facts were concealed.
Justice Alwi said Tan had also failed to prove malice when the statements were made and that Chow’s defence of qualified privilege also applied as he was entitled to publicly respond to Tan’s resignation letter.
The court ordered Tan to pay RM50,000 in costs.
Tan filed the suit against Chow in January 2024 over Chow’s statements in connection with his resignation as a trustee of the Silver Jubilee Home for the Aged.
Chow made the remarks at two press conferences held at Chow’s office at Komtar in Penang on Dec 1, 2023 and Dec 6, 2023 and his statements were carried by the press.
At that material time, both Tan and Chow were trustees of the Penang and Province Wellesley Silver Jubilee Fund, a corporation established to maintain the Silver Jubilee home.
The High Court in Penang had dismissed Tan’s suit, prompting him to appeal to the Court of Appeal.
At the Court of Appeal today, lawyers K. Kirubakaran, Kek Boon Wei and Lee Wen Qian appeared for Tan while lawyer Cheah Eng Soon represented Chow. — Bernama

Title: Jakim to hold special prayers tonight as haze blankets Malaysia
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 26 — The Department of Islamic Development Malaysia (Jakim) will hold a Solat Hajat (special prayer of needs) at three mosques under its supervision tonight following the haze currently affecting the country.
Jakim director-general Datuk Dr Sirajuddin Suhaimee said the prayers would be held after Maghrib prayers at the National Mosque here, as well as Putra Mosque and Tuanku Mizan Zainal Abidin Mosque in Putrajaya.
He called on Muslims to join in and pray to Allah SWT for protection, health, safety and peace in facing this trial.
“May Allah SWT protect all Malaysians from any harm, safeguard our health and safety and restore conditions in affected areas,” he said in a statement today.
He said the Solat Hajat was in line with a decree by the Sultan of Pahang, Al-Sultan Abdullah Ri’ayatuddin Al-Mustafa Billah Shah, calling on all Malaysians to pray and seek Allah SWT’s help for the well-being of those affected, as well as a call by Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Religious Affairs) Dr Zulkifli Hasan to undertake the effort.
As of 8 am today, 17 areas in six states, namely Sarawak, Selangor, Negeri Sembilan, Johor, Melaka and Perak, as well as Kuala Lumpur and Putrajaya, recorded unhealthy Air Pollutant Index (API) readings. — Bernama

Title: MMEA clears Karakit-Kudat ferry after passenger safety concerns go viral
Article:
KUDAT, Aug 26 — The Malaysian Maritime Enforcement Agency (MMEA) Kudat Zone conducted an inspection of a ferry operating on the Karakit-Kudat route on Sunday following information circulating on social media concerning the safety and comfort of its passengers.
The inspection found no offences or breaches of regulations involving the ferry, while the number of passengers on board was within the permitted limit and did not exceed its approved capacity.
MMEA Kudat Zone Director Maritime Commander Hasbullah Omar said the inspection was conducted to ensure ferry operators consistently complied with safety requirements and relevant regulations.
“MMEA will continue to conduct monitoring and inspections from time to time to ensure maritime transport operators comply with regulations and prioritise passenger safety,” he said.
He said MMEA Kudat Zone took all information and complaints received from the public seriously, particularly those concerning passenger safety and vessel operations in Kudat waters.
He also advised the public to obtain verified information from the authorities before drawing any conclusions regarding issues circulating on social media.
The public are also encouraged to channel information concerning maritime safety or suspicious activities at sea by calling the emergency line at 999 or the Kudat Maritime Zone Operations Centre at 088-611858 for immediate action. — Daily Express

Title: Calls grow for Sabah to widen pork imports beyond Denmark and France as prices climb to RM18 per kg
Article:
KOTA KINABALU, Aug 26 — Pork prices in Sabah have risen to RM17.50 or RM18 per kg, prompting calls for wider import sources and stronger efforts to reduce food costs in the State.
Agriculture and Food Security Deputy Minister Datuk Chan Foong Hin said the increase was partly linked to Sabah’s limited sources of imported pork, with the State currently allowing imports from only Denmark and France.
He said the Federal Government approved frozen pork imports from 11 countries, including Australia, the United States, Brazil, Thailand, Canada, Belgium, Ireland and Spain.
However, Sabah and Sarawak have the authority to decide whether such imports are allowed into their respective states.
“Sabah only allows two countries – Denmark and France,” he said, adding that all imported pork sources must first undergo audits and meet food safety requirements.
He said the situation was different in the peninsula, where the introduction of chilled pork from Thailand had helped create greater competition and contributed to a decline in prices over the past six months.
According to him, the Government’s decision to allow chilled pork from Thailand was intended to provide consumers with a more competitive alternative while encouraging local producers to remain competitive.
Chan, who is also Kota Kinabalu MP, said Sabah’s geographical distance from Europe could also contribute to higher prices, as imported pork may have to pass through Singapore before reaching the State.
He linked Sabah’s limited supply sources to the smuggling of frozen meat and other food products across the State’s borders.
He said recent operations by the Sabah border authorities had uncovered cases involving frozen chicken and pork brought into the State through channels outside the authorised veterinary route.
He stressed that food safety standards remained important but said diversification of import sources could help address pricing and supply concerns.
Chan said Sabah also faced longer-term challenges involving pig farming, including environmental compliance, pollution controls and the need to modernise farming operations.
He said the State needed more modern and responsible pig farming facilities, while operators at a facility in Tongod had yet to begin operations despite infrastructure being completed in 2018.
For the short term, he urged the State Government to look into ways to bring down the cost of living, particularly food prices, which he said were higher in Sabah than in other parts of Malaysia.
He said he had been in contact with the State authorities to discuss the possibility of diversifying pork import sources.
He also planned to hold another pork sale in conjunction with the coming Mooncake Festival to help ease the burden on the non-Muslim community. — Daily Express
More pork import sources needed to bring down Sabah prices, says deputy minister

Title: High Court refuses to strike out RM200,000 fee refund suit against Sri Ram’s estate
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 26 — The High Court has dismissed an application by the widow of the late Federal Court judge Datuk Seri Gopal Sri Ram to strike out a lawsuit seeking the return of RM200,000 in legal fees paid to him before his death.
Justice Alice Loke ruled that plaintiff Khoo Gee Tat’s claim was not “obviously unsustainable” and should proceed to a full hearing on its merits,
FMT
reported.
Khoo engaged Sri Ram in 2022 as lead counsel to represent his son, Adrian Khoo, in a criminal appeal before the Court of Appeal.
A pro forma invoice issued by Sri Ram’s law firm, Messrs Sri Ram, fixed the legal fees at RM349,800, after which Gee Tat made four instalment payments totalling RM200,000.
Sri Ram died on Jan 29, 2023, before concluding the appeal, which the appellate court eventually heard and disposed of on Dec 5 that year.
Gee Tat subsequently sought a refund of the RM200,000 on the grounds that the agreed legal services were never fully rendered.
He filed the present lawsuit against Sri Ram’s widow, Chandra Sri Ram, in her capacity as the executor and trustee of the late judge’s estate.
Chandra applied to strike out the suit, contending among other arguments that Gee Tat was not Sri Ram’s client and consequently lacked the legal standing to sue.
Loke rejected that argument, holding that Gee Tat had directly engaged Sri Ram, paid the retainer fee, received the invoice, and maintained communication with him throughout the appeal.
In her 10-page judgment, Loke noted that the definition of “client” under the Legal Profession Act 1976 could encompass Gee Tat.
She also dismissed assertions that the claim was frivolous, vexatious, or barred under the principle of res judicata (previously decided matter).
Loke held that the competing arguments over whether the RM200,000 was refundable involved substantial legal and factual disputes requiring detailed examination, making the case unsuitable for summary disposal.
Lawyers Ng Choon Kiat and Ahmad Nur Zharif Rosdi represented Gee Tat, while Alvin Oh, Thooi Zi Hui, and Sew Chang Peng acted for Chandra, who has filed an appeal against the decision.

Title: Woman, 62, found bound and dead in Sandakan, cops nab 10 suspects, youngest aged 10
Article:
SANDAKAN, Aug 26 — Ten people, including two believed to be the main suspects, have been detained following the discovery of a 62-year-old woman’s decomposing body inside her house in Tanah Merah, Jalan Leila, here.
District Police Chief ACP George Abd Rahman said the woman, believed to have been living alone, was found with her hands tied behind her back and her head covered with a piece of cloth inside the house’s toilet.
He said police were alerted at 8.10pm on Aug 19 after a foul smell was reported coming from the two-storey wooden house.
“Police arrived at 8.45pm and found the body of a woman in the toilet, with her hands tied behind her back and her head covered with a cloth,” he said.
The victim is believed to have died several days earlier.
George said the victim was identified through documents found in the house.
Police subsequently made several arrests within 24 hours, comprising five males and five females aged from 10 to 39.
Three are Philippine nationals while seven are Malaysians and all 10 are related. George said two were identified as main suspects.
“Investigations found a dispute over payment for renovation work at the victim’s house, as well as unhappiness over an increase in rent of the house occupied by the two suspects,” he said, adding the case is being investigated under Section 302 of the Penal Code for murder. — Daily Express

Title: Sabah to upgrade SICC-Menera Kinabalu stretch, ditch permanent bridge plan
Article:
KOTA KINABALU, Aug 26 — The State Government plans to upgrade the entire stretch from the Sabah International Convention Centre (SICC) towards Menara Kinabalu, making the permanent replacement of the bridge at Tanjung Lipat unnecessary.
Deputy Chief Minister I cum State Works and Utilities Minister Datuk Seri Dr Joachim Gunsalam said this when asked whether there were any plans to repair the bridge.
The bridge located at Jalan Tun Fuad Stephens at Km 2.85 along Likas Bay was closed after being found unsafe for use in late July.
The Works Department moved quickly to install a temporary Bailey bridge at the site, with installation taking several weeks.
More than an on-ground activation, Hotlink Prepaid Pasti Mampu Belanja Makan celebrated the spirit of Sabah’s Geng Bijak Berbajet, people who know that spending wisely doesn’t mean settling for less, but finding smarter ways to enjoy more.
The Bailey bridge was opened to the public last Friday.
“The temporary bridge is completed, but we have to limit the weight to a certain amount because we are also concerned about safety when it comes to vehicles that are too heavy,” he said.
“We actually have plans to redo the whole stretch from SICC up towards Menara Kinabalu.
“So, there is no point for us to build a permanent bridge at this point because there is a plan to upgrade the road,” he said.
Regarding concerns raised about warning markers near SICC and Hakka Hall that have reportedly been hit by vehicles, Dr Joachim said the markers serve to alert drivers whose vehicles exceed the permitted height or weight limits.
“The markers are actually meant to warn the public not to use the road if their vehicle is too tall or too heavy,” he said.
Recently, a representative of the roll-on roll-off (ro-ro) trailer operators, Masrul Guding, said the alternative route provided was difficult and unsafe for the approximately 22-metre-long trailers.
He said the situation affected the delivery of new vehicles from Kota Kinabalu Port. — Daily Express

Title: Putrajaya approves 367 projects worth RM9b to replace dilapidated schools
Article:
TAPAH, Aug 26 — The government has approved 367 projects to redevelop dilapidated school buildings worth RM9 billion nationwide from 2023 to 2026.
Deputy Education Minister Wong Kah Woh said the allocation involved 86 projects worth RM1.711 billion in 2023, 78 projects totalling RM1.825 billion in 2024, 124 projects costing RM4.1 billion in 2025 and 79 projects worth RM1.384 billion in 2026.
“This is the largest amount by any government over a four-year period. The higher allocations and approvals for more projects are aimed at expediting the redevelopment of the affected school buildings for the safety of students.
“This also demonstrates the continued commitment under the leadership of Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim to ensure that dilapidated school premises are addressed in stages,” he said.
He said this when met after attending the handover ceremony for the Education Ministry’s Dilapidated School Replacement Building Project at Sekolah Jenis Kebangsaan Cina (SJKC) Coldstream here today.
On the completion period for the projects, Wong said it depended on the scope, specifications and location of each project, with implementation generally taking two years after approval and the appointment of a contractor.
Touching on the construction of the replacement building at SJKC Kampung Coldstream, he said the RM2.9 million project began on May 24, 2024 and was fully completed on Aug 6.
He said the building was equipped with various modern facilities, including four comfortable classrooms, two new toilet units and an open hall for the use of students and teachers at the school.
“The building is also equipped with other facilities, including 120 sets of new chairs and tables, as well as Smart TV units supplied by the state education department (JPN) and district education office (PPD),” he said.
He said with these facilities, students could enjoy a conducive learning environment, while the school’s special-purpose rooms, which had previously been used as temporary classrooms, could be restored to their original functions. — Bernama

Title: Penang State Museum smashes 2026 visitor targets in first month after reopening
Article:
GEORGE TOWN, Aug 26 — The Penang State Museum on Farquhar Street has recorded a surge of 47,638 visitors in just 29 days following its reopening last month, exceeding initial expectations.
State tourism and creative economy committee chairman Wong Hon Wai said that the museum exceeded its original target for the rest of the year within just 30 days. The high turnout follows a nine-year closure for extensive restoration works.
“Our original target was 30,000 visitors by December, but in one month we have already exceeded 47,000 visitors,” Wong said at a press conference at the museum today.
The museum’s peak attendance occurred on Aug 9, with 3,750 visitors in a single day. On average, the site attracts 1,000 visitors on weekdays and up to 4,000 on weekends. Wong expects a baseline of at least 1,500 visitors per month once paid admission is implemented.
The current surge is partly attributed to the free-entry period, which began upon the museum's reopening on July 24 and will end on Aug 31.
Starting Sept 1, admission fees will be introduced: RM5 for MyKad holders and RM3 for children (aged five to 12), senior citizens, and persons with disabilities.
Non-Malaysians will be charged RM20 for adults and RM10 for children, seniors, and persons with disabilities. Children under five enter for free.
As a gesture of celebration, free admission will return on Sept 15 and 16 to mark Malaysia Day and the anniversary of Penang Hill’s recognition as a Unesco Biosphere Reserve.
To modernise the visitor experience, the reopened museum now incorporates digital elements and augmented reality, specifically designed to engage school students and younger audiences.
Due to space constraints at the two-storey Farquhar Street building, the state will open a museum branch next month at 57 Macalister Road. This new site will house exhibits that could not fit into the main gallery.
The state museum building holds significant historical weight, having been constructed in 1816. It formerly housed the Penang Free School and Hutchings School before its conversion into a museum in 1964.
Visitors can still see the foundations of a section of the building that was bombed during World War II, which has been preserved as a showcase at the entrance.

Title: Stop shifting goalposts on Tabung Haji RCI, PKR Youth tells Akmal
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 26 — PKR Youth information chief Danish Hairudin has accused Umno Youth chief Datuk Dr Akmal Saleh of shifting his stance on the Lembaga Tabung Haji (TH) Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI) because its findings and resulting arrests failed to match his political narrative.
Danish said Akmal, previously among the most vocal figures demanding the report’s release, was now attempting to “move the goalposts”.
“Must everyone follow Akmal and Umno’s lead until we get the answer that Umno wants?” Danish asked, noting the inquiry was not formed under Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim’s administration.
Danish argued that if Umno, which sits in the unity government, sees shortcomings in the report, it should raise and debate them in Parliament.
He added that any fresh evidence should be investigated “regardless of who is involved,” insisting no one should be shielded.
He also urged Umno and Akmal not to ignore uncomfortable findings in the report, such as “creative accounting”, severe governance lapses, and investment losses of up to 100 per cent.
“Reveal everything. Debate everything,” Danish said, warning against repeating playbooks from the 1MDB scandal where core issues were “obscured and whitewashed.”
He also said that Tabung Haji belongs to millions of depositors, not political parties.
“If you truly want the truth, accept the truth in its entirety. Do not keep searching for an RCI until you find the answer you like.”
Earlier, Akmal made a social media post defending calls for a fresh RCI into TH’s asset transfer to Urusharta Jamaah Sdn Bhd (UJSB) under the first Pakatan Harapan administration.
Akmal was responding to PKR Youth chief Muhammad Kamil Abdul Munim, who questioned the need for another inquiry, while also citing Pasir Gudang MP Hassan Abdul Karim’s stance: “If we want to reveal it, we reveal everything, not just partially.”

Title: Kuching airport repairs underway after storm damages ceiling
Article:
KUCHING, Aug 26 — Repair works have been carried out at Kuching International Airport (KIA) following damage to part of its external ceiling structure caused by severe weather on Tuesday.
Malaysia Airports, in an update posted on its official Facebook page, said the affected area had been secured to allow the repair works to be carried out safely.
“Repair works at KIA are underway on the section of the external ceiling structure affected by the severe weather earlier today (Tuesday),” it said.
It added that airport operations were continuing as normal.
“We appreciate the patience and cooperation of passengers and airport users while these works are being completed,” Malaysia Airports said.
On Tuesday afternoon, a section of the roof at the arrival area of KIA was damaged following strong winds and heavy rain that swept through Kuching.
The incident was among several reports of weather-related damage in the city, including uprooted trees in various areas. — The Borneo Post

Title: Coroner walks out during Zara Qairina inquest after saying ‘Am I not fair enough?’ twice
Article:
KOTA KINABALU, Aug 26 — The Coroner’s Court hearing the inquest into the death of Zara Qairina Mahathir saw a tense moment today when Coroner Judge Amir Shah Amir Hassan suddenly stood and left his bench after twice asking, “Am I not fair enough?” during questioning of consultant psychiatrist Dr Wong Haw Huo.
The inquest was subsequently paused for about 50 minutes before resuming.
The exchange took place while Wong, the 75th witness in the inquest, was being questioned by lawyer Datuk Ram Singh, counsel for one of the teenagers charged in the bullying case involving Zara Qairina.
The lawyer had repeatedly asked Wong to provide direct answers to his questions, including on the cause of Zara Qairina’s fall and whether the teenager was alone before the incident.
Datuk Rizwandean M. Borhan, representing Zara Qairina’s mother, then remarked that Ram’s questioning of Wong appeared harsh.
Ram then responded: “Sir, don’t use the word harsh on me. In the past and towards the end, they (other counsels) were also very harsh, but this is very important for us. Very important.”
Judge Amir Shah then said: “But this is an inquest, not a trial.”
Ram responded: “I’m not saying it’s a trial, Sir. I mean let’s be fair to us. Let’s be fair.”
Judge Amir Shah then asked: “Am I not fair? Am I not fair enough?”
Ram replied: “You are fair, Sir,” prompting the coroner to repeat: “Am I not fair enough?”
Ram then said: “No, Sir. Let’s not get agitated with this. He (Wong) is going round and round and explaining.”
After the 50-minute pause, Ram apologised to the court, saying he had not intended his earlier remarks to be construed as questioning the fairness of the proceedings.
Ram also said the coroner’s decision to leave the courtroom had come as a shock to him as counsel in the inquest, adding that he hoped such an incident would not recur. Rizwandean also tendered an apology.
Judge Amir Shah accepted the apologies from Ram and Rizwandean, but reminded counsel to remain cautious and professional in conducting themselves throughout the inquest.
He also apologised, saying it was the first time in his 21 years of service that he had walked out from the bench.
“I should also apologise to you all for bursting out, and this is the first time that I walked out from the bench, with a little pain in my chest. Let’s not be emotional. Let’s be professional. That is the main aim for this inquest,” he said.
Moving on, Wong told the court that the last student to encounter Zara Qairina before the fall has been regarded as an important person in assessing the teenager’s mental state shortly before the incident.
Wong said interviewing the student would have enabled the psychiatrists to better understand Zara Qairina’s conversation, appearance, speech, behaviour and emotional condition at the time.
He said such information was important in establishing Zara Qairina’s mental state, including her understanding of the possible consequences of her actions.
Zara Qairina died at Queen Elizabeth Hospital on July 17, 2025, a day after she was found unconscious in a drain near her school hostel at about 4 am. — Bernama

Title: Missing Penang Kafa teacher due to wed in September turns up in Kedah
Article:
GEORGE TOWN, Aug 26 — A male Quran and Fardu Ain (Kafa) teacher who was reported missing since last Saturday after leaving his home at an apartment in Sungai Ara near here was found safe in Kampung Bukit Payong, Pokok Sena, Kedah early this morning.
Barat Daya police chief ACP Anuwal Ab Wahab said following further investigations, police managed to trace Mohamad Hijazi Zamri, 26, at a house in Kampung Bukit Payong.
“Checks found that the man was in good condition and had not sustained any physical injuries. He was subsequently taken to the Bayan Lepas police station for further action before being handed over to his family,” he said in a statement today.
He said police expressed their appreciation to all parties who had assisted in efforts to locate the man and advised the public not to make any speculation or disseminate unverified information regarding the incident.
Meanwhile, Mohamad Hijazi’s father, Zamri Saidin, 53, when contacted, also expressed his appreciation to all parties who helped search for his son, as well as those who continued to pray for the safety of the eldest of his seven children.
He said he received a call from an individual who was also Mohamad Hijazi’s friend, informing him that he had found his son and asking to speak to him over the phone to verify his voice.
Previously, police said investigations found that the man had asked his mother for permission to go to Surau Al-Muttaqin in Lilitan Sungai Ara on a blue Yamaha LC135 motorcycle. However, he did not return home and could not be contacted by his family. — Bernama

Title: Look beyond racial and political lines this Merdeka, urges Sultan of Selangor
Article:
SHAH ALAM, Aug 26 — The Sultan of Selangor, Sultan Sharafuddin Idris Shah, has urged Malaysians to use this year’s National Day celebrations to reinforce national unity by looking past racial, religious, and political divides.
His Royal Highness made the call after officiating a flag-raising ceremony at Dataran Selangor on Wednesday. The event marked the start of the official flag-flying period, running until September 17 in conjunction with Merdeka Day and Malaysia Day..
The Sultan had earlier consented to the Jalur Gemilang being hoisted at the Selangor State Flagpole throughout the commemorative period.
“Although we differ in race, religion, language, political ideology and background, the Jalur Gemilang reminds us that we remain citizens of the same nation,” the Sultan said.
“This flag belongs to all of us. We must be proud because it is a symbol of national unity.”
The Sultan stressed that the spirit of Merdeka must go beyond ceremonial pageantry, calling on citizens to honour those who have dedicated their lives to bridging communal divides.
He also highlighted the importance of nurturing the younger generation with mutual respect and appreciation for diverse cultures, races, and faiths.
Directing his message to political leaders, the Sultan delivered a pointed reminder that national leaders shoulder a vital duty in safeguarding unity.
“Leaders and politicians must set an example by practising moderation, tolerance and compassion, and must not use political, racial or religious differences as a reason to divide the people,” he said.
The Sultan observed that while hoisting thousands of flags across the country during the independence month is straightforward, the true test lies in cultivating a nation where every Malaysian genuinely feels respected, valued, and proud of their citizenship.
He said that the Jalur Gemilang draws no distinction between ethnic communities, whether Malay, Chinese, Indian, Kadazan-Dusun, Iban, or others, nor does it discriminate across religious traditions including Islam, Buddhism, Christianity, and Hinduism.
“Independence is not merely something to be celebrated, and the flag is not merely something to be flown,” the Sultan said.
“Their true value lies in our collective ability to defend a nation whose people can live together in peace, mutual respect and unity.”

Title: WhatsApp ‘boss’ scam leaves Terengganu car dealership RM452,000 poorer
Article:
KUALA TERENGGANU, Aug 26 — A car dealership company suffered losses of RM452,000 after its clerk fell victim to a phone scam syndicate.
Kuala Terengganu district police chief ACP Azli Mohd Noor said the 50-year-old finance clerk received a WhatsApp message last Monday from a suspect whom she believed to be the company owner.
He said the suspect instructed the victim to provide the company’s account balance and make three separate transfers totalling RM452,000 to three different accounts on the same day.
“The following day, the suspect instructed the victim to make an additional transfer of RM235,000 to another account.
“The victim, who became suspicious after receiving numerous transaction requests, contacted the company owner by phone to verify the matter, only to learn that her employer had not given such instructions,” he said.
Azli said the victim lodged a police report at 11.19 am yesterday after realising she had been duped, and the case was being investigated under Section 420 of the Penal Code. — Bernama

Title: Penang SPM candidate targeted in sexual cyberbullying gets Education Dept support, protection
Article:
GEORGE TOWN, Aug 26 — The Penang State Education Department (JPNPP) has assured that necessary measures are in place to ensure the safety and wellbeing of an Sijil Pelajaran Malaysia (SPM) candidate who was subjected to harassment through WhatsApp here.
Its director Mohamad Dziauddin Mat Saad said appropriate steps had been taken to protect the identity of the 17-year-old student and ensure that the incident did not disrupt her preparations for the SPM examination.
“The situation has now eased and the school will ensure that the student can attend classes without any disruption while providing her with the necessary support and guidance.
“We would like to assure parents that the school is taking steps to safeguard the student’s wellbeing,” he told reporters after assessing the school’s preparedness for haze at Sekolah Kebangsaan Sungai Gelugor here today.
He said a police report had also been lodged over the case, with investigations currently being conducted at the school and several locations linked to it.
Mohamad Dziauddin said the school had also advised the student to seek guidance and counselling to help her manage her emotions and focus on her SPM preparations.
He said JPNPP would continue to monitor the case and work with the school and parents to safeguard the student’s safety and wellbeing.
A mother, who wished to be identified only as Nur, 46, recently urged the authorities to expedite investigations into those allegedly responsible for repeatedly subjecting her 17-year-old daughter to sexual cyberbullying.
The woman said her second child, an SPM candidate, had experienced emotional distress after her face, name, class and phone number were allegedly circulated through obscene posters and fake social media accounts since April. — Bernama

Title: One China policy: Understanding Malaysia’s position on Beijing and Taipei
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 26 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim’s remarks on Taiwan have brought renewed attention to Malaysia’s One China policy and its relations with Beijing and Taipei.
In an August 2026 interview with
Al Jazeera
, the Pakatan Harapan chairman said: “I see Taiwan as part of China, period”.
When asked about Beijing’s refusal to rule out military force for reunification, Anwar drew a comparison with Malaysia, saying that if a Malaysian province attempted to break away, he would use force to protect national unity.
The remarks were welcomed by Beijing and criticised by Taipei.
Anwar later reiterated that Malaysia prefers a peaceful resolution and that its position under the One China policy remains unchanged since 1974.
What is the ‘One China’ framework?
There are two interpretations of the framework.
One is Beijing’s “One China Principle”, which asserts that there is only one China, that the People’s Republic of China (PRC) is its sole legal government, and that Taiwan is an “inalienable part” of Chinese territory. Beijing views cross-strait relations as an internal affair, according to news reports citing international relations analysts.
Malaysia’s “One China Policy”, meanwhile, was established through a 1974 Joint Communiqué that formally established diplomatic relations with Beijing, making Malaysia the first Asean country to do so. The communiqué was signed by then prime minister, the late Tun Abdul Razak, and his Chinese counterpart Zhou Enlai on May 31 that year.
The policy means that while Kuala Lumpur officially recognises the PRC as the sole legal government of China and acknowledges Beijing’s position on Taiwan, it does not formally endorse Beijing’s claims over the island.
Putrajaya’s One China policy also emphasises the importance of maintaining peace and stability across the Taiwan Strait.
Beijing and Taipei’s response
Chinese Foreign Ministry spokesperson Lin Jian commended Anwar, saying his remarks reflected international consensus and supported Beijing’s position on Taiwan.
Taiwan’s Foreign Ministry rejected the remarks, saying Taiwan is not a province of China and expressing concern that such rhetoric could legitimise the use of military coercion. Taiwanese officials also warned the comments could affect investor confidence.
Will Anwar’s comments affect ties with Taiwan?
Malaysia has no official diplomatic ties with Taiwan, but both sides maintain robust unofficial economic, cultural and technological links.
The Malaysian Friendship and Trade Centre, Taipei (MFTC), established in 1987, serves as Malaysia’s representative office in Taipei, while Taiwan is represented by the Taipei Economic and Cultural Office in Kuala Lumpur. In the absence of formal diplomatic relations, the two offices perform many functions typically associated with embassies.
Whether Taipei will follow its statement with further action remains to be seen, while reactions in Taiwanese and Chinese media have been mixed.
Analysts have suggested Anwar’s remarks could dampen Taiwanese investor appetite if Malaysia is perceived as leaning more heavily towards Beijing, particularly as technology companies value geopolitical predictability.
A columnist in
China Times
noted that Taipei’s responses to similar statements by Southeast Asian countries have generally been limited to official rebuttals, arguing Taiwan is more likely to continue pursuing its “New Southbound Policy” to diversify its economic footprint away from mainland China.
In 2025, total trade between Malaysia and Taiwan reached US$54.49 billion, up from US$38.63 billion in 2024, according to a note on the Ministry of Foreign Affairs’ website.
Taiwan was Malaysia’s fourth-largest trading partner, accounting for 7.6 per cent of Malaysia’s total trade.

Title: Three more nabbed over illegal race on Malaysia-Singapore Second Link
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 26 — Police have arrested three more men in Kuala Lumpur over a brazen illegal street race that brought traffic to a halt along the Malaysia-Singapore Second Link.
Kulai police chief Tan Seng Lee said the latest arrests bring the total number of individuals detained in connection with the incident to 11,
Kosmo
reported.
The three suspects will be produced in court for a remand application.
“Further investigation into this case is ongoing under Section 42(1) of the Road Transport Act 1987,” he said.
Police had earlier rounded up eight men on Sunday, including a motorsport influencer, obtaining a four-day remand order to facilitate investigations.
The incident unfolded at around 7am on Sunday along the stretch from KM33 (Senai Toll Exit) to KM31 (Johor Premium Outlets Exit).
A 30-second viral video sparked widespread public outrage after showing the group blocking morning motorists across the expressway to clear the route for the race.

Title: Bersatu leadership approves two Pahang reps’ move to back Umno menteri besar
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 26 — Two Bersatu assemblymen in Pahang have thrown their support behind Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Wan Rosdy Wan Ismail of Umno, with the party's top leadership signalling its backing for the move.
Kuala Sentul assemblyman Datuk Jasri Jamaluddin and Lepar assemblyman Datuk Mohd Yazid Mohd Yunus — Bersatu's only two elected representatives in the 42-seat Pahang assembly — signed a memorandum of understanding with Wan Rosdy, pledging their backing for his administration until the next state election, expected by early 2028.
In a media statement issued the same day, Bersatu vice-president Datuk Seri Ahmad Faizal Azumu confirmed that the two ADUNs had informed the party leadership of their intention beforehand and left the final call to the party.
“The Bersatu political bureau, chaired by Tan Sri Muhyiddin Yassin, president of Bersatu, discussed the matter from all angles and, in principle, supports the action.
“This decision was made to ensure political stability in the state of Pahang and to ensure that the welfare of the people in both of the respective constituencies receives due attention and representation from the Pahang state government,” Ahmad Faizal said.
Jasri and Yazid echoed this reasoning in their own joint statement, saying the understanding reached with the menteri besar would help ensure development and welfare priorities in Kuala Sentul and Lepar are not neglected.
They added that they would continue discharging their duties as elected representatives and cooperate with the state administration,
FMT
reported.
Wan Rosdy has headed the Pahang state government since a hung assembly emerged from the November 2022 state election. That election left Perikatan Nasional as the single largest bloc, edging out the ruling Barisan Nasional coalition by one seat, but Wan Rosdy was reappointed a week later at the helm of a BN–Pakatan Harapan coalition government.
Bersatu, as part of Perikatan Nasional, had held two of PN's seats in the assembly, alongside 15 from PAS.
With Jasri and Yazid's declared support, Wan Rosdy's administration now commands backing from 27 of the assembly's 42 seats.
